items.title: Analyzer projections of a two-dimensional polarisation space and their overlaps
items.statement:
## Statement

Let $V$ be a two-dimensional complex inner product space with inner product
linear in the first argument ([[def-inner-product-space]],
[[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]]), and let $(e_{1},e_{2})$ be an
orthonormal basis of $V$
([[def-orthonormal-family-complete-orthonormal-system-and-hilbert-basis]]).
For $\theta\in\mathbb R$ put
$$e_{\theta}:=\cos\theta\,e_{1}+\sin\theta\,e_{2},\qquad e_{\theta}^{\perp}:=-\sin\theta\,e_{1}+\cos\theta\,e_{2},$$
and for $x\in V$ define
$$P_{\theta}x:=\langle x,e_{\theta}\rangle\,e_{\theta},\qquad P_{\theta}^{\perp}x:=\langle x,e_{\theta}^{\perp}\rangle\,e_{\theta}^{\perp}.$$
Then:

(a) for every $\theta$ the maps $P_{\theta}$ and $P_{\theta}^{\perp}$ are
orthogonal projections on $V$ with ranges $\mathbb Ce_{\theta}$ and
$\mathbb Ce_{\theta}^{\perp}$ ([[def-hilbert-orthogonal-projection]],
[[lem-orthogonal-projection-is-linear-self-adjoint-contractive]]), one has
$P_{\theta}+P_{\theta}^{\perp}=I$ and $P_{\theta}P_{\theta}^{\perp}=0$, and
$$P_{\theta}P_{\theta}=P_{\theta}=P_{\theta}^{*},\qquad P_{\theta}P_{\theta}^{\perp}=P_{\theta}^{\perp}P_{\theta}=0;$$

(b) for all real $\varphi,\theta$ the unit vectors
$\psi_{\varphi}:=\cos\varphi\,e_{1}+\sin\varphi\,e_{2}$ satisfy
$$\langle e_{\theta},\psi_{\varphi}\rangle=\cos(\theta-\varphi),\qquad \langle\psi_{\varphi},P_{\theta}\psi_{\varphi}\rangle=\|P_{\theta}\psi_{\varphi}\|^{2}=|\langle e_{\theta},\psi_{\varphi}\rangle|^{2}=\cos^{2}(\theta-\varphi),$$
and $\langle\psi_{\varphi},P_{\theta}^{\perp}\psi_{\varphi}\rangle=\sin^{2}(\theta-\varphi)$;

(c) the assignments $\theta\mapsto P_{\theta}$ and $\theta\mapsto
P_{\theta}^{\perp}$ are $2\pi$-periodic, $P_{\theta+\pi}=P_{\theta}$ and
$P_{\theta+\pi/2}=P_{\theta}^{\perp}$, and for every $z\in\mathbb C$ and
$x\in V$ one has $P_{\theta}(zx)=zP_{\theta}x$ and
$\|P_{\theta}(z\psi_{\varphi})\|^{2}/\|z\psi_{\varphi}\|^{2}=\cos^{2}(\theta-\varphi)$
whenever $z\ne0$; in particular the number $\cos^{2}(\theta-\varphi)$ depends
only on the ray $[\psi_{\varphi}]$, not on the representative;

(d) the pair $(P_{\theta},P_{\theta}^{\perp})$ is a two-element family of
mutually orthogonal projections on $V$ with $P_{\theta}+P_{\theta}^{\perp}=I$,
its outcomes $+1$ and $-1$ have spectral projections $P_{\theta}$ and
$P_{\theta}^{\perp}$ for the bounded self-adjoint operator $P_{\theta}$ in the
sense that the eigenspace of $P_{\theta}$ at eigenvalue $1$ is
$\mathbb Ce_{\theta}$ and the eigenspace at eigenvalue $0$ is
$\mathbb Ce_{\theta}^{\perp}$.

No physical interpretation of $V$, of the pair $(e_{1},e_{2})$ or of the
projections $P_{\theta}$ is asserted.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** the two-dimensional complex inner product space $V$ with inner product linear in the first argument, the orthonormal basis $(e_{1},e_{2})$ of $V$, the vectors $e_{\theta},e_{\theta}^{\perp},\psi_{\varphi}\in V$ and the maps $P_{\theta},P_{\theta}^{\perp}:V\to V$.

[F1] **Inner product and norm.** For all $x,y\in V$ and $a,b\in\mathbb C$, $\langle ax+by,z\rangle=a\langle x,z\rangle+b\langle y,z\rangle$ and $\langle x,ay+bz\rangle=\overline a\langle x,y\rangle+\overline b\langle x,z\rangle$; $\langle x,x\rangle\ge0$ with equality only for $x=0$; and $\|x\|^{2}=\langle x,x\rangle$ ([[def-inner-product-space]], [[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]]).

[F2] **Orthonormality.** $\langle e_{i},e_{j}\rangle=\delta_{ij}$ for $i,j\in\{1,2\}$ ([[def-orthonormal-family-complete-orthonormal-system-and-hilbert-basis]]).

[F3] **Expansion in an orthonormal basis.** Since $(e_{1},e_{2})$ is a complete orthonormal family of the two-dimensional space $V$, every $x\in V$ satisfies $x=\langle x,e_{1}\rangle e_{1}+\langle x,e_{2}\rangle e_{2}$ and $\|x\|^{2}=|\langle x,e_{1}\rangle|^{2}+|\langle x,e_{2}\rangle|^{2}$ ([[thm-parseval-equivalences-for-a-complete-orthonormal-family]]).

[F4] **Orthogonal projections.** A bounded linear map $P:V\to V$ with $P^{2}=P=P^{*}$ is the orthogonal projection onto its range, its range is a closed subspace, and $\|Px\|\le\|x\|$ ([[def-hilbert-orthogonal-projection]], [[lem-orthogonal-projection-is-linear-self-adjoint-contractive]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct; compute the overlaps of the displayed vectors from the orthonormality of $(e_{1},e_{2})$ and verify the projection identities.

**Given:** The data of the statement and [F1]-[F4].

1.1 [The rotated pairs are orthonormal] By [F1] and [F2], $\langle e_{\theta},e_{\theta}\rangle=\cos^{2}\theta+\sin^{2}\theta=1$, $\langle e_{\theta}^{\perp},e_{\theta}^{\perp}\rangle=\sin^{2}\theta+\cos^{2}\theta=1$ and $\langle e_{\theta},e_{\theta}^{\perp}\rangle=-\cos\theta\sin\theta+\sin\theta\cos\theta=0$; hence $(e_{\theta},e_{\theta}^{\perp})$ is an orthonormal family of the two-dimensional space $V$, therefore an orthonormal basis of $V$. [F1, F2, algebra]

1.2 [Overlaps and the cosine identity] By [F1] and [F2], $\langle e_{\theta},\psi_{\varphi}\rangle=\cos\theta\cos\varphi+\sin\theta\sin\varphi=\cos(\theta-\varphi)$ and $\langle e_{\theta}^{\perp},\psi_{\varphi}\rangle=-\sin\theta\cos\varphi+\cos\theta\sin\varphi=\sin(\varphi-\theta)$. Then $\langle\psi_{\varphi},P_{\theta}\psi_{\varphi}\rangle=\langle\psi_{\varphi},\langle\psi_{\varphi},e_{\theta}\rangle e_{\theta}\rangle=|\langle\psi_{\varphi},e_{\theta}\rangle|^{2}=\cos^{2}(\theta-\varphi)$ because $\cos(\theta-\varphi)$ is real, and $\|P_{\theta}\psi_{\varphi}\|^{2}=|\cos(\theta-\varphi)|^{2}\|e_{\theta}\|^{2}=\cos^{2}(\theta-\varphi)$; similarly $\langle\psi_{\varphi},P_{\theta}^{\perp}\psi_{\varphi}\rangle=\sin^{2}(\theta-\varphi)$. This is (b). [F1, F2, algebra]

2.1 [The projections are orthogonal projections] For $x\in V$, $P_{\theta}x=\langle x,e_{\theta}\rangle e_{\theta}$, so $P_{\theta}(P_{\theta}x)=\langle\langle x,e_{\theta}\rangle e_{\theta},e_{\theta}\rangle e_{\theta}=\langle x,e_{\theta}\rangle\langle e_{\theta},e_{\theta}\rangle e_{\theta}=P_{\theta}x$ by [F1] and step 1.1: $P_{\theta}^{2}=P_{\theta}$. For the adjoint, $\langle P_{\theta}x,y\rangle=\langle\langle x,e_{\theta}\rangle e_{\theta},y\rangle=\langle x,e_{\theta}\rangle\langle e_{\theta},y\rangle=\langle x,\langle y,e_{\theta}\rangle e_{\theta}\rangle=\langle x,P_{\theta}y\rangle$ for all $x,y$, so $P_{\theta}^{*}=P_{\theta}$; the same computation with $e_{\theta}^{\perp}$ in place of $e_{\theta}$ gives $P_{\theta}^{\perp\,2}=P_{\theta}^{\perp}=P_{\theta}^{\perp\,*}$. By [F4] both are the orthogonal projections onto their ranges $\mathbb Ce_{\theta}$ and $\mathbb Ce_{\theta}^{\perp}$. [F1, step 1.1, F4, algebra]

3.1 [Complementarity] By step 1.1 and [F3] applied to the orthonormal basis $(e_{\theta},e_{\theta}^{\perp})$, every $x\in V$ satisfies $x=\langle x,e_{\theta}\rangle e_{\theta}+\langle x,e_{\theta}^{\perp}\rangle e_{\theta}^{\perp}=P_{\theta}x+P_{\theta}^{\perp}x$; hence $P_{\theta}+P_{\theta}^{\perp}=I$. Applying $P_{\theta}$ to the same expansion and using $P_{\theta}e_{\theta}^{\perp}=\langle e_{\theta}^{\perp},e_{\theta}\rangle e_{\theta}=0$ gives $P_{\theta}P_{\theta}^{\perp}=0$, and likewise $P_{\theta}^{\perp}P_{\theta}=0$. Since $P_{\theta}=I-P_{\theta}^{\perp}$ and $\mathbb Ce_{\theta}\cap\mathbb Ce_{\theta}^{\perp}=\{0\}$ by orthogonality of the nonzero vectors $e_{\theta},e_{\theta}^{\perp}$, the eigenspace of $P_{\theta}$ at eigenvalue $1$ is $\mathbb Ce_{\theta}$ and at eigenvalue $0$ is $\mathbb Ce_{\theta}^{\perp}$; this proves (a) and (d). [F1, F3, step 1.1, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 [Periodicity and phase invariance] Since $e_{\theta+\pi}=-e_{\theta}$ and $e_{\theta+\pi/2}=e_{\theta}^{\perp}$, the identities $P_{\theta+\pi}=P_{\theta}$ and $P_{\theta+\pi/2}=P_{\theta}^{\perp}$ follow from the definition of $P_{\theta}$ and [F1]; in particular $P_{\theta}$ is $2\pi$-periodic. For $z\ne0$ and the unit vector $\psi_{\varphi}$ one has $\|z\psi_{\varphi}\|^{2}=|z|^{2}$, and $P_{\theta}(z\psi_{\varphi})=zP_{\theta}\psi_{\varphi}$ by linearity of $x\mapsto\langle x,e_{\theta}\rangle$ in the second argument of [F1]; hence $\|P_{\theta}(z\psi_{\varphi})\|^{2}/\|z\psi_{\varphi}\|^{2}=\|P_{\theta}\psi_{\varphi}\|^{2}=\cos^{2}(\theta-\varphi)$ by step 1.2. This proves (c) and completes the proof. [F1, step 1.2, algebra] ∎

## Remarks

- **What the lemma is not.** The lemma is finite-dimensional linear algebra:
  no dynamics, no measurement postulate and no physical identification of
  $e_{\theta}$ with an apparatus direction is asserted. The physical reading of
  the projections as the outcome structure of a polarisation analyser is fixed
  in [[def-nrqm-photons-framework-fixed-mode-polarization-model]].
- **The identity $\cos^{2}(\theta-\varphi)$ is classical and quantum at once.**
  The same projection formula governs the classical transverse field amplitude
  and the quantised polarisation amplitude; the comparison, and the reason that
  the coincidence of the numbers does not establish field quantisation, is the
  subject of the companion examples page of this pair, which is not a
  prerequisite of this lemma.

items.title: Restricted momentum and energy multipliers of the transverse one-photon space
items.statement:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), the choice hypotheses of
the cited multiplication and spectral items. On
$L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{3})$ ([[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]])
put
$$\mathfrak h:=\Bigl\{f:\ k\cdot f(k)=0\ \text{for almost every }k\Bigr\},$$
a closed subspace of $L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{3})$, and write
$\Pi(k):=\mathrm{id}-|k|^{-2}kk^{\mathsf T}$ for $k\ne0$, $\Pi(0):=0$, so that
$\mathfrak h=\operatorname{ran}M_{\Pi}$ with $M_{\Pi}$ the bounded
multiplication by $\Pi$ ([[def-hilbert-orthogonal-projection]],
[[lem-orthogonal-projection-is-linear-self-adjoint-contractive]]). Let
$c,\hbar>0$ with $c$ in $\mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-1}$ and $\hbar$ in
$\mathrm J\,\mathrm s$, and for $j\in\{1,2,3\}$ and $m\in\{\hbar k_{j},\ \hbar c|k|\}$
define
$$D(M_{m}^{\mathfrak h}):=\{f\in\mathfrak h:\ \textstyle\int_{\mathbb R^{3}}m(k)^{2}\|f(k)\|_{\mathbb C^{3}}^{2}\,d^{3}k<\infty\},\qquad M_{m}^{\mathfrak h}f:=mf .$$
Then for each such $m$:

(a) $M_{m}^{\mathfrak h}$ is a densely defined self-adjoint operator on the
Hilbert space $\mathfrak h$ ([[def-hilbert-space]],
[[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]), and it is the
restriction to $\mathfrak h$ of the self-adjoint multiplier $M_{m}$ on
$L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{3})$ of
[[thm-nrqm-composites-real-multipliers-and-free-bounded-potential-operators]];

(b) its spectral projection-valued measure $E_{m}$ is given by
$$E_{m}(B)=M_{\mathbf 1_{m^{-1}(B)}}\bigr|_{\mathfrak h}\qquad(B\subseteq\mathbb R\ \text{Borel}),$$
and for every unit $f\in\mathfrak h$ the outcome law $B\mapsto\|E_{m}(B)f\|^{2}$
is the push-forward of the finite measure $|f|^{2}\,d^{3}k\big|_{\mathfrak h}$
under $k\mapsto m(k)$; in particular for $m=\hbar k_{j}$ it is the push-forward
under $k\mapsto\hbar k_{j}$ and for $m=\hbar c|k|$ it is the push-forward under
$k\mapsto\hbar c|k|$ ([[def-projection-valued-measure]],
[[lem-unbounded-pvm-integral-is-well-defined-and-closed]]);

(c) $M_{m}^{\mathfrak h}$ has no eigenvalues: for no $\lambda\in\mathbb R$ is
there a nonzero $f\in D(M_{m}^{\mathfrak h})$ with $M_{m}^{\mathfrak h}f=\lambda f$;

(d) for every unit $f\in D(M_{m}^{\mathfrak h})$ one has
$$\operatorname{Var}_{f}(M_{m}^{\mathfrak h}):=\|M_{m}^{\mathfrak h}f\|^{2}-\langle M_{m}^{\mathfrak h}f,f\rangle^{2}>0;$$
consequently no unit vector of $\mathfrak h$ has a sharp $m$-value.

The identifications of $\mathfrak h$ and of these multipliers with physical
transverse photons, momenta or energies are not asserted here; they are a
separate model assignment outside this lemma.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** the Axioms of Countable Choice and of Choice, the constants $c,\hbar>0$, the transverse subspace $\mathfrak h=\operatorname{ran}M_{\Pi}$, the Borel sets $B\subseteq\mathbb R$, the functions $m\in\{\hbar k_{j},\hbar c|k|\}$ and the operators $M_{m}^{\mathfrak h}$.

[F1] **Full-space multiplier.** For a real measurable finite-valued $a:\mathbb R^{3}\to\mathbb R$ the componentwise multiplier $M_{a}u:=au$ on $D(M_{a})=\{u\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{3}):au\in L^{2}\}$ is self-adjoint: the scalar statement is [[thm-nrqm-composites-real-multipliers-and-free-bounded-potential-operators]] clause (a), applied to each of the three components of $u$.

[F2] **Spectral measure of a multiplier.** Let $(X,\Sigma,\mu)$ be $\sigma$-finite with $\mu(X)>0$, $m:X\to\mathbb R$ measurable and finite a.e., $H=L^{2}(X,\mu;\mathbb C)$ and $M_{m}$ as in [F1]. Then $E(B):=M_{\mathbf 1_{m^{-1}(B)}}$ is the spectral projection-valued measure of $M_{m}$, and for a unit vector $\psi\in H$ one has $\|E(B)\psi\|^{2}=\int_{m^{-1}(B)}|\psi|^{2}\,d\mu$ ([[lem-nrqm-observables-l2-multiplication-spectral-measure]] clauses (b), (c)).

[F3] **PVM integrals.** Let $E$ be a projection-valued measure on a Hilbert space $K$ and $f$ real-valued measurable. Then $f(E)=\int f\,dE$ is self-adjoint with domain $D(f(E))=\{x:\int f^{2}\,dE_{x}<\infty\}$, where $dE_{x}$ is the scalar measure of $E$ at $x$, and $\|f(E)x\|^{2}=\int f^{2}\,dE_{x}$; moreover bounded measurable functions with $|g_{n}|\le C|f|$ and $g_{n}\to f$ pointwise satisfy $g_{n}(E)x\to f(E)x$ for every $x\in D(f(E))$ ([[def-unbounded-integral-against-a-pvm]], [[lem-unbounded-pvm-integral-is-well-defined-and-closed]]).

[F4] **Hilbertian projections.** $\mathfrak h=\operatorname{ran}M_{\Pi}$ is a closed linear subspace of $L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{3})$ with the restricted inner product, and $M_{\Pi}$ is the orthogonal projection onto it; multiplication operators by functions of $k$ commute with $M_{\Pi}$ ([[def-hilbert-orthogonal-projection]], [[lem-orthogonal-projection-is-linear-self-adjoint-contractive]], [[thm-nrqm-composites-real-multipliers-and-free-bounded-potential-operators]]).

[F5] **Null level sets of the momentum components.** For $j\in\{1,2,3\}$ and $\lambda\in\mathbb R$ the set $\{k\in\mathbb R^{3}:\hbar k_{j}=\lambda\}$ is the graph of a constant, hence Lebesgue measurable, function over $\mathbb R^{2}$ and is Lebesgue null ([[cor-graph-of-a-measurable-function-is-lebesgue-null]]).

[F6] **Null spheres.** For $\lambda\in\mathbb R$ the set $\{k\in\mathbb R^{3}:\hbar c|k|=\lambda\}$ is empty when $\lambda<0$ and otherwise the sphere of radius $\lambda/(\hbar c)$, which is Lebesgue null: by the polar-coordinates formula $\int_{\mathbb R^{3}}g\,d\lambda_{3}=\int_{0}^{\infty}\int_{S^{2}}g(r\omega)r^{2}\,d\sigma(\omega)\,dr$ for Borel measurable $g\ge0$, applied to $g=\mathbf 1_{\{|k|=r_{0}\}}$ the inner integrand vanishes for every $r\ne r_{0}$, and $\{r_{0}\}$ is a countable, hence $\lambda_{1}$-null, subset of $(0,\infty)$ ([[thm-polar-coordinates-formula-for-lebesgue-measure]], [[prop-countable-subsets-of-rn-are-lebesgue-null]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct; restrict the full-space multiplier to the invariant closed subspace, identify the restricted spectral measure, and use the nullity of the level sets to exclude eigenvectors.

**Given:** The data of the statement and [F1]-[F6].

1.1 [Restriction of the spectral measure] Let $m$ be one of the two displayed functions; both are real, measurable and finite-valued. By [F4] the multiplier $M_{m}$ commutes with $M_{\Pi}$, so $E(B)=M_{\mathbf 1_{m^{-1}(B)}}$ (componentwise) commutes with $M_{\Pi}$ for every Borel set $B$ and therefore maps $\mathfrak h$ into itself: for $f\in\mathfrak h$ one has $E(B)f=\mathbf 1_{m^{-1}(B)}f\in\mathfrak h$ because transversality holds pointwise. Thus $E_{\mathfrak h}(B):=E(B)|_{\mathfrak h}$ is a family of projections on $\mathfrak h$ with $E_{\mathfrak h}(B)^{2}=E_{\mathfrak h}(B)=E_{\mathfrak h}(B)^{*}$, $E_{\mathfrak h}(\varnothing)=0$, $E_{\mathfrak h}(\mathbb R)=\mathrm{id}_{\mathfrak h}$, and $\sigma$-additivity and strong convergence inherited from $E$; hence $E_{\mathfrak h}$ is a projection-valued measure on $\mathfrak h$. [F2, F4, algebra]

1.2 [No eigenvalues] Let $\lambda\in\mathbb R$ and let $f\in D(M_{m}^{\mathfrak h})$ satisfy $M_{m}^{\mathfrak h}f=\lambda f$, that is $m(k)f(k)=\lambda f(k)$ for almost every $k$. Then $f=0$ almost everywhere on $\{k:m(k)\ne\lambda\}$, so $f$ is supported in $N_{\lambda}:=\{k:m(k)=\lambda\}$ up to a null set. For $m=\hbar k_{j}$ the set $N_{\lambda}$ is null by [F5]; for $m=\hbar c|k|$ it is null by [F6]. In both cases $f=0$ almost everywhere, hence $f=0$ in $L^{2}$. This proves (c). [F5, F6, algebra]

2.1 [The restricted integral is the restricted multiplier] By [F3] applied to $E_{\mathfrak h}$ and the real function $\lambda\mapsto\lambda$ the operator $A:=\int\lambda\,dE_{\mathfrak h}(\lambda)$ is self-adjoint with domain $\{f\in\mathfrak h:\int\lambda^{2}\,dE_{\mathfrak h,f}(\lambda)<\infty\}$. For every $g\in\mathfrak h$ and Borel $B$ we have $\langle E_{\mathfrak h}(B)g,g\rangle=\int_{m^{-1}(B)}\|g(k)\|^{2}\,d^{3}k$: the scalar statements of [F2] applied to the three components of $g$ combine by sesquilinearity, and the unit case extends by scaling in $g$, so the scalar measure $E_{\mathfrak h,g}$ is the push-forward of $\|g\|^{2}\,d^{3}k$ under $k\mapsto m(k)$; hence $\int\lambda^{2}\,dE_{\mathfrak h,f}(\lambda)=\int m(k)^{2}\|f(k)\|^{2}\,d^{3}k$ by the change-of-variables formula for a push-forward measure against the Borel function $\lambda\mapsto\lambda^{2}$, the two sides agreeing on indicators of Borel sets and extending by linearity and monotone convergence. Therefore $D(A)=\{f\in\mathfrak h:\int m^{2}\|f\|^{2}\,d^{3}k<\infty\}=D(M_{m}^{\mathfrak h})$. [F2, F3, F4, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 [Identification on the domain] Let $f\in D(A)$ and put $m_{n}:=m\mathbf 1_{\{|m|\le n\}}$ for $n\ge1$; then $|m_{n}|\le|m|$ and $m_{n}\to m$ pointwise, so [F3] gives $m_{n}(E_{\mathfrak h})f\to Af$. For $g\in\mathfrak h$ the bounded operator $m_{n}(E_{\mathfrak h})$ satisfies $\langle m_{n}(E_{\mathfrak h})g,g\rangle=\int m_{n}\,dE_{\mathfrak h,g}=\int m_{n}(k)\|g(k)\|^{2}\,d^{3}k=\langle m_{n}g,g\rangle$ by the push-forward description of step 2.1; both operators are bounded and self-adjoint and their quadratic forms agree, so $m_{n}(E_{\mathfrak h})=M_{m_{n}}|_{\mathfrak h}$: the bounded functional calculus of the restricted multiplier is multiplication by $m_{n}$. The convergence $m_{n}f\to mf$ in $L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{3})$ holds by dominated convergence, since $\|m_{n}f-mf\|^{2}\le4m^{2}\|f\|^{2}$ is integrable under $f\in D(A)$; its limit $mf$ lies in $\mathfrak h$ because transversality is preserved pointwise, and lies in $D(A)$ because $\int m^{2}\|f\|^{2}<\infty$. Hence $Af=mf=M_{m}^{\mathfrak h}f$ for every $f\in D(A)$; conversely if $f\in D(M_{m}^{\mathfrak h})$ then $\int m^{2}\|f\|^{2}=\|mf\|^{2}<\infty$, so $f\in D(A)$. Therefore $A=M_{m}^{\mathfrak h}$ with the displayed domain, and (a) and (b) follow. [F1, F2, F3, step 1.1, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 [Positive variance] Let $f\in\mathfrak h$ be a unit vector in $D(M_{m}^{\mathfrak h})$ and put $\mu:=\langle M_{m}^{\mathfrak h}f,f\rangle$, a real number because $M_{m}^{\mathfrak h}$ is self-adjoint. Then $$\|M_{m}^{\mathfrak h}f\|^{2}-\langle M_{m}^{\mathfrak h}f,f\rangle^{2}=\|(M_{m}^{\mathfrak h}-\mu I)f\|^{2}\ge0,$$ and equality holds exactly when $(M_{m}^{\mathfrak h}-\mu I)f=0$, that is when $f$ is an eigenvector of $M_{m}^{\mathfrak h}$ with eigenvalue $\mu$. By step 1.2 no nonzero eigenvector exists, so the left-hand side is strictly positive. This proves (d) and completes the proof. [step 1.2, algebra] ∎

## Remarks

- **Choice hypotheses.** Both cited suppliers (the multiplication spectral
  measure and the PVM-integral lemma) are stated with the Axioms of Countable
  and Dependent Choice; the Axiom of Choice enters only through those citations
  and is carried explicitly. The nullity computations use Countable Choice.
- **What fails for sharp modes.** Step 1.2 says that the sharp-mode idealisation
  of the radiation model is not a state vector of the sector: a normalisable
  one-photon vector never has an exact frequency or an exact momentum component.
  The plane-wave labels $k$ are parameters of the spectral representation, not
  normalisable states.

items.title: The fixed-mode isometry of Fock space and the transfer of number and ladder operators
items.statement:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $H$ be a complex
Hilbert space ([[def-hilbert-space]],
[[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]]) with completed tensor powers
$H^{\otimes n}$, symmetric projections $P_+^{(n)}$, Fock space $F(H)$, sector
projections $\Pi_n$, number operator $N$ and maximal creation and annihilation
operators $A_\pm(f)$ as in
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-hilbert-direct-sum-construction]],
[[lem-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-fock-sector-projections]],
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-number-operator-domain]] and
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-closed-adjoint-sector-domains]]. Fix a unit
vector $\varphi\in H$. Write $\varphi^{\otimes0}:=1\in\mathbb C$ and
$\varphi^{\otimes n}:=\varphi\otimes\cdots\otimes\varphi\in H^{\otimes n}$ for
$n\ge1$, and define
$$U_\varphi:F(\mathbb C)\to F(H),\qquad U_\varphi e_n:=(0,\dots,0,\varphi^{\otimes n},0,\dots)$$
with the entry in coordinate $n$, extended linearly. Then:

(a) each $\varphi^{\otimes n}$ is a unit vector of
$\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}$; the family $(\varphi^{\otimes n})_{n\in\mathbb N}$
is orthonormal in $F(H)$, and $U_\varphi$ is a linear isometry of
$F(\mathbb C)$ onto the closed subspace
$\overline{\operatorname{span}}\{\varphi^{\otimes n}:n\in\mathbb N\}$
([[def-orthonormal-family-complete-orthonormal-system-and-hilbert-basis]],
[[thm-parseval-equivalences-for-a-complete-orthonormal-family]],
[[def-bounded-linear-operator]]);

(b) for every $\psi=(\psi_n)_{n\in\mathbb N}\in F(\mathbb C)$ and every $n$,
$$\Pi_nU_\varphi\psi=U_\varphi\Pi_n'\psi,\qquad \|U_\varphi\psi\|^{2}=\sum_{n\in\mathbb N}|\psi_n|^{2}=\|\psi\|^{2},$$
where $\Pi_n'$ is the Fock sector projection of $F(\mathbb C)$; and for every
$\psi\in D(N')$ one has $U_\varphi\psi\in D(N)$ with
$$NU_\varphi\psi=U_\varphi N'\psi ;$$

(c) for every $\psi\in D(A_\pm(1))$ one has $U_\varphi\psi\in D(A_\pm(\varphi))$
and
$$A_\pm(\varphi)U_\varphi\psi=U_\varphi A_\pm(1)\psi ;$$
in particular for every $z\in\mathbb C$ the coherent vector
$\psi_z=e^{-|z|^{2}/2}\sum_n\frac{z^{n}}{\sqrt{n!}}e_n$ of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-fixed-mode-number-law]] satisfies
$U_\varphi\psi_z\in D(A_-(\varphi))$ and $A_-(\varphi)U_\varphi\psi_z=z\,U_\varphi\psi_z$;

(d) for the transverse case $H=\mathfrak h$ of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-transverse-continuum-free-fock-hamiltonian]]
with $\varepsilon(k)=\hbar c|k|$, $H_f=\bigoplus_nT_n$, and a unit
$\varphi\in\mathfrak h\cap D(\varepsilon_{\mathfrak h})$ (so that
$\varepsilon\varphi\in\mathfrak h$), one has
$$\langle H_fU_\varphi e_n,U_\varphi e_n\rangle=n\,\langle\varepsilon\varphi,\varphi\rangle\qquad(n\in\mathbb N),$$
and for every $\psi\in F(\mathbb C)$ with $\sum_nn^{2}|\psi_n|^{2}<\infty$
$$\langle H_fU_\varphi\psi,U_\varphi\psi\rangle=\Bigl(\sum_{n\in\mathbb N}n|\psi_n|^{2}\Bigr)\langle\varepsilon\varphi,\varphi\rangle=\langle N'\psi,\psi\rangle\,\langle\varepsilon\varphi,\varphi\rangle ;$$
if moreover $\varphi\in D(\varepsilon_{\mathfrak h}^{2})$, then
$$\langle T_n\varphi^{\otimes n},\varphi^{\otimes n}\rangle=n\,\langle\varepsilon\varphi,\varphi\rangle,\qquad \langle T_n^{2}\varphi^{\otimes n},\varphi^{\otimes n}\rangle=n\,\langle\varepsilon^{2}\varphi,\varphi\rangle+n(n-1)\,\langle\varepsilon\varphi,\varphi\rangle^{2}.$$

No physical interpretation of the isometry, of the vectors
$U_\varphi e_n$, or of the transferred operators is asserted.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** the complex Hilbert space $H$, its Fock space $F(H)$ with sectors $\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}$, projections $\Pi_n$, number operator $N$ and maximal operators $A_\pm(f)$, the unit vector $\varphi\in H$, the map $U_\varphi$, a vector $\psi=(\psi_n)\in F(\mathbb C)$, and in part (d) the transverse space $\mathfrak h$, the energy multiplier $\varepsilon$ and the operator $H_f=\bigoplus_nT_n$.

[F1] **Sectors and coordinate embeddings.** For $n\ge1$ the vector $\iota_n(u):=(0,\dots,0,u,0,\dots)$ with $u\in\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}$ lies in $F(H)$, $\|\iota_n(u)\|=\|u\|$, and the ranges of distinct $\iota_n$ are orthogonal; the same formula with $n=0$ and $\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(0)}=\mathbb C$ gives the vacuum embedding, so the embedding is defined for every $n\in\mathbb N$; for $x,y\in F(H)$ one has $\langle x,y\rangle=\sum_n\langle x_n,y_n\rangle$ and $\|x\|^{2}=\sum_n\|x_n\|^{2}$ ([[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-hilbert-direct-sum-construction]] clauses (a),(c),(d), [[lem-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-fock-sector-projections]] clauses (a),(b)).

[F2] **Symmetric tensors.** $P_+^{(n)}$ is the orthogonal projection onto $\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}$; for $u\in H$ the elementary tensor $u^{\otimes n}=u\otimes\cdots\otimes u$ satisfies $P_+^{(n)}u^{\otimes n}=u^{\otimes n}$, $\|u^{\otimes n}\|=\|u\|^{n}$, and $\langle u^{\otimes n},v^{\otimes n}\rangle=\langle u,v\rangle^{n}$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-permutation-sector-projections]] clause (c), [[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]] clause (b)).

[F3] **Number operator.** $N$ is self-adjoint with $D(N)=\{\psi:\sum_nn^{2}\|\psi_n\|^{2}<\infty\}$ and $N\Pi_n=n\Pi_n$ on the sector, i.e. $(Nx)_n=nx_n$; the Fock space is the orthogonal direct sum of the sector ranges ([[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-number-operator-domain]] clauses (a),(b), [[lem-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-fock-sector-projections]] clause (c)).

[F4] **Maximal creation and annihilation operators.** $A_+(f)$ and $A_-(f)$ are closed linear respectively conjugate-linear operators with domains $D(A_+(f))=\{\psi:\sum_n(n+1)\|P_+^{(n+1)}(f\otimes\psi_n)\|^{2}<\infty\}$ and $D(A_-(f))=\{\psi:\sum_n(n+1)\|\Psi_f^{(n)}(\psi_{n+1})\|^{2}<\infty\}$, and on them $(A_+(f)\psi)_n=\sqrt nP_+^{(n)}(f\otimes\psi_{n-1})$, $(A_-(f)\psi)_n=\sqrt{n+1}\Psi_f^{(n)}(\psi_{n+1})$; the contraction maps satisfy $\Psi_f^{(n)}(u_1\otimes\cdots\otimes u_{n+1})=\langle u_1,f\rangle u_2\otimes\cdots\otimes u_{n+1}$ ([[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-closed-adjoint-sector-domains]], [[lem-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-creation-contraction-bounds]] clauses (a),(b)).

[F5] **Fixed-mode oscillator coefficients.** For $F(\mathbb C)$ with orthonormal basis $(e_n)$ and the operators $A_\pm(1)$ one has $A_+(1)e_n=\sqrt{n+1}e_{n+1}$, $A_-(1)e_n=\sqrt n\,e_{n-1}$ for $n\ge1$ and $A_-(1)e_0=0$; for every $z\in\mathbb C$ the vector $\psi_z=e^{-|z|^{2}/2}\sum_n\frac{z^{n}}{\sqrt{n!}}e_n$ is unit and satisfies $A_-(1)\psi_z=z\psi_z$ ([[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-fixed-mode-number-law]] clauses (a),(b)).

[F6] **Transverse Fock data.** For the transverse space $\mathfrak h$ and $\varepsilon=\hbar c|k|$, the operators $T_n$ on $\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}$ are self-adjoint with $T_n\psi=\varepsilon_n\psi$, $\varepsilon_n(k_1,\dots,k_n)=\sum_{i=1}^{n}\varepsilon(k_i)$, and $H_f=\bigoplus_nT_n$ is self-adjoint with domain $\{\psi:\sum_n\|T_n\psi_n\|^{2}<\infty\}$; under the Euclidean identification of $\mathfrak h^{\otimes n}$ with a subspace of $L^{2}((\mathbb R^{3})^{n};(\mathbb C^{3})^{\otimes n})$, the multiplier $\varepsilon_n$ is symmetric and commutes with all permutation unitaries, so $\varepsilon_n$ preserves $\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}$ ([[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-transverse-continuum-free-fock-hamiltonian]] clauses (a),(b),(c), [[lem-nrqm-composites-permutation-sector-projections]] clause (c), [[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]] clause (b)).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct; identify $F(\mathbb C)$ inside $F(H)$ along the coefficient expansion in the single mode $\varphi$, check the isometry and the sectorially diagonal operators coefficientwise, and evaluate the energy expectation on the mode sector by symmetry of the tensor integrals.

**Given:** The data of the statement and [F1]-[F6].

1.1 [The powers of $\varphi$ are orthonormal sector vectors] For $n\ge0$ put $\Phi_n:=\varphi^{\otimes n}$, with $\Phi_0:=1$. By [F2] with $u=\varphi$ and $\|\varphi\|=1$ one has $\|\Phi_n\|=1$ for every $n$, $P_+^{(n)}\Phi_n=\Phi_n$, and $\langle\Phi_n,\Phi_n\rangle=\prod_{i=1}^{n}\langle\varphi,\varphi\rangle=1$; for $m\ne n$ the pairing $\langle\Phi_m,\Phi_n\rangle$ vanishes because $\Phi_m$ is supported in the direct-sum coordinate $m$ and $\Phi_n$ in coordinate $n$, and the inner product of $F(H)$ is the sum of the coordinate pairings by [F1]. Hence $(\Phi_n)_{n\in\mathbb N}$ is an orthonormal family with $\Phi_n\in\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}$ for every $n$. [F1, F2, algebra]

2.1 [The isometry] Define $U_\varphi$ on the finite linear span of $(e_n)$ by $U_\varphi e_n=\Phi_n$ and extend by linearity; by step 1.1, $\|U_\varphi\psi\|^{2}=\sum_n|\psi_n|^{2}=\|\psi\|^{2}$ for every finite combination, so $U_\varphi$ is isometric on the dense finite-particle subspace $F_0(\mathbb C)$ of [[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-hilbert-direct-sum-construction]] clause (c) and extends uniquely to an isometry $U_\varphi:F(\mathbb C)\to F(H)$ with the same norm identity for all $\psi\in F(\mathbb C)$ ([[def-bounded-linear-operator]], [[thm-parseval-equivalences-for-a-complete-orthonormal-family]]). Its range is the closed linear span of $(\Phi_n)$, since an isometry maps the closed span of an orthonormal family onto the closed span of its image and the image family is orthonormal; this proves (a). [F1, F2, algebra]

2.2 [Ladder transfer] Let $f:=\varphi$ and let $\psi\in D(A_+(1))$, so that $\sum_n(n+1)|(A_+(1)\psi)_n|^{2}<\infty$. For the vector $U_\varphi\psi$ with coefficients $\psi_n$ the defining sum of $A_+(\varphi)$ is $\sum_n(n+1)\|P_+^{(n+1)}(\varphi\otimes\psi_n\Phi_n)\|^{2}$; by [F2] and bilinearity of the tensor product, $\varphi\otimes\psi_n\Phi_n=\psi_n\Phi_{n+1}$, and $P_+^{(n+1)}\Phi_{n+1}=\Phi_{n+1}$; hence the sum equals $\sum_n(n+1)|\psi_n|^{2}$, which is finite precisely when $\psi\in D_1(G)$ for $G=F(\mathbb C)$, i.e. when the coefficient vector lies in the weighted space of [F4]; since $D(A_+(1))\subseteq D_1$ by [F4], $U_\varphi\psi\in D(A_+(\varphi))$. Its $n$-th coordinate is $\sqrt nP_+^{(n)}(\varphi\otimes\psi_{n-1}\Phi_{n-1})=\sqrt n\,\psi_{n-1}\Phi_n$, while the $n$-th coordinate of $U_\varphi A_+(1)\psi$ is $(A_+(1)\psi)_{n-1}\Phi_n=\sqrt n\,\psi_{n-1}\Phi_n$ by [F5]; hence $A_+(\varphi)U_\varphi\psi=U_\varphi A_+(1)\psi$. The same computation with [F4]'s contraction formula gives $(A_-(\varphi)U_\varphi\psi)_n=\sqrt{n+1}\,\Psi_\varphi^{(n)}(\psi_{n+1}\Phi_{n+1})=\sqrt{n+1}\,\psi_{n+1}\Phi_n=(U_\varphi A_-(1)\psi)_n$; the domain sum $\sum_n(n+1)|\psi_{n+1}|^{2}$ is finite exactly when $\psi\in D_1\supseteq D(A_-(1))$, so the identification holds on $D(A_-(1))$. Applying it to $\psi_z$ of [F5] gives the final assertion of (c). [F4, F5, step 1.1, algebra]

2.3 [Energy expectation] Assume now $H=\mathfrak h$ and $\varphi$ unit with $\varepsilon\varphi\in\mathfrak h$; write $\bar\varepsilon:=\langle\varepsilon\varphi,\varphi\rangle$. For fixed $n$, $\Phi_n=\varphi^{\otimes n}\in\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}$ and, by [F6], $T_n\Phi_n=\varepsilon_n\Phi_n$; using the Euclidean identification and the symmetry of $\varepsilon_n$ under the permutation action, the iterated $L^{2}$ integral gives $$\langle T_n\Phi_n,\Phi_n\rangle=\int_{(\mathbb R^{3})^{n}}\Bigl(\sum_{i=1}^{n}\varepsilon(k_i)\Bigr)\prod_{i=1}^{n}\|\varphi(k_i)\|_{\mathbb C^{3}}^{2}\,d^{3}k_1\cdots d^{3}k_n=n\,\bar\varepsilon\,\|\varphi\|^{2(n-1)}=n\,\bar\varepsilon,$$ each of the $n$ summands contributing the same product $\bar\varepsilon\|\varphi\|^{2(n-1)}$ by Tonelli's theorem, the product measure being $\sigma$-finite and the integrand nonnegative; this is finite because $\varepsilon\varphi\in L^{2}$ and $\varphi\in L^{2}$ give $\int\varepsilon\|\varphi\|^{2}\le\|\varepsilon\varphi\|\,\|\varphi\|<\infty$. Therefore for a finite combination the sector-diagonal form of $H_f$ (clause (c) of [F6]) gives $\langle H_fU_\varphi\psi,U_\varphi\psi\rangle=\sum_n|\psi_n|^{2}\,n\bar\varepsilon$; the general case $\sum_nn^{2}|\psi_n|^{2}<\infty$ follows by approximation with truncations in the graph norm of $H_f$ (both sides are continuous under this approximation, the left because $H_f$ is closed and self-adjoint, the right by dominated convergence). This proves the first two displays of (d). [F3, F6, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 [Sector and number transfer] For $\psi=\sum_m\psi_me_m$ in the dense span and fixed $n$, $\Pi_nU_\varphi\psi=\psi_n\Phi_n=U_\varphi(\psi_ne_n)=U_\varphi\Pi_n'\psi$; since both sides are bounded in $\psi$ and the span is dense, the identity extends to all $\psi\in F(\mathbb C)$, and the norm identity is step 2.1. For $\psi\in F(\mathbb C)$ the coefficient vector of $U_\varphi\psi$ is again $(\psi_n)$, so $\sum_nn^{2}\|(U_\varphi\psi)_n\|^{2}=\sum_nn^{2}|\psi_n|^{2}$: $U_\varphi\psi\in D(N)$ exactly when $\psi\in D(N')$, and then $(NU_\varphi\psi)_n=n\psi_n\Phi_n=(U_\varphi N'\psi)_n$ for every $n$ by [F3]. This proves (b). [F1, F3, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 [Second energy moment] If $\varphi\in D(\varepsilon^{2})$, expand $\varepsilon_n^{2}=\sum_{i}\varepsilon(k_i)^{2}+\sum_{i\ne j}\varepsilon(k_i)\varepsilon(k_j)$ and integrate term by term against $\prod_i\|\varphi(k_i)\|^{2}$; by Tonelli's theorem, applied to the nonnegative summands on the $\sigma$-finite product space, the $n$ diagonal terms each contribute $\langle\varepsilon^{2}\varphi,\varphi\rangle$ and the $n(n-1)$ off-diagonal terms each contribute $\bar\varepsilon^{2}$, so $\langle T_n^{2}\Phi_n,\Phi_n\rangle=n\langle\varepsilon^{2}\varphi,\varphi\rangle+n(n-1)\bar\varepsilon^{2}$. All these numbers are finite: $\varphi\in D(\varepsilon^{2})$ gives $\|\varepsilon\varphi\|<\infty$ and $\|\varepsilon^{2}\varphi\|<\infty$, and $\bar\varepsilon\le\|\varepsilon\varphi\|\|\varphi\|$. This proves the third display of (d) and completes the proof. [F6, step 1.1, algebra] ∎

## Remarks

- **Scope.** The lemma is a coefficientwise statement about an orthonormal
  family in a Fock space; it does not assert that a fixed mode is an energy
  eigenstate. In fact the energy transfer is only an expectation statement:
  $H_f$ does not preserve the span of the $\varphi^{\otimes n}$ unless
  $\varepsilon\varphi$ is a multiple of $\varphi$, which for the transverse
  continuum fails for every nonzero $\varphi$ by
  [[lem-nrqm-photons-transverse-restricted-momentum-and-energy-multipliers]]
  clause (c).
- **Choice hypotheses.** Only the Axioms of Countable Choice and of Choice
  inherited from the cited Fock space items are used; no further choice is
  introduced.

items.title: Radiation extension of the framework: transverse mode and photon assignments
items.statement:
## Postulate

Adopt, as an additional model assumption of the framework on this page and its
consumers, the following radiation extension. It is adopted together with the
state and composition postulate P1, the observable and probability postulate P2,
the kinematics and massive-particle model postulate P5, the identical-particle
and spin postulate P6 and the preparation and apparatus discipline P7
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]), in the space vocabulary of
[[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]], the observable vocabulary of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]], the species and
sector vocabulary of
[[def-nrqm-identical-particles-framework-species-sectors-and-preparations]],
and the units and dimensions of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]].
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice, the choice
hypotheses of the cited Fock space mathematics ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

**(i) Fixed propagation-mode one-photon polarisation model.** For a declared
propagation mode, described by a nonzero wavevector label
$k_{0}\in\mathbb R^{3}\setminus\{0\}$ read in $\mathrm m^{-1}$ in a declared
inertial chart ([[def-nrqm-framework-inertial-frames]]), the model assigns a
two-dimensional complex internal space, the **transverse polarisation space**
of the mode: the complex span of an orthonormal pair $(v_{1},v_{2})$ of vectors
of $\mathbb C^{3}$ satisfying $k_{0}\cdot v_{1}=k_{0}\cdot v_{2}=0$, with the
standard Hermitian form. Unit rays of this space are the model's **one-photon
polarisation preparations** of the mode. This assignment is an idealised
manifestation of the abstract Born/state framework on a finite-dimensional
internal factor; it is not a spatial wave function of a massive particle, not a
model of a photon position, and not the massive one-particle Hamiltonian of P5
with mass set to zero: the framework's massive family has no massless
self-adjoint member obtained as $m\downarrow0$
([[cex-nrqm-framework-zero-mass-has-no-self-adjoint-limit]]), and no such limit
is used here.

**(ii) Quantised transverse radiation sector.** The model assigns to the free
radiation a **bosonic species** in the sense of P6, whose one-particle space is
the transverse space
$$\mathfrak h:=\Bigl\{f\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{3}):\ k\cdot f(k)=0\ \text{for almost every }k\Bigr\}$$
with the $L^{2}$ inner product; its $n$-particle sector is
$\mathfrak H_{n}^{+}=\operatorname{ran}P_{+}^{(n)}$ and its radiation state
space is the bosonic Fock space $F(\mathfrak h)=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}\mathfrak H_{n}^{+}$
([[def-nrqm-identical-particles-framework-species-sectors-and-preparations]],
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-hilbert-direct-sum-construction]]). The
statistics choice "bosonic" is an empirical model assignment of P6 clause (iii)
and is not derived here; it is motivated by the photon's observed
indistinguishability and integer spin but is adopted, not deduced.

**(iii) Mode assignments of frequency, energy and momentum.** In the declared
inertial chart, each free mode label $k\in\mathbb R^{3}\setminus\{0\}$ is
assigned the **angular frequency** $\omega(k):=c|k|$ in $\mathrm s^{-1}$, the
**photon energy** $E(k):=\hbar\omega(k)=\hbar c|k|$ in joules and the
**photon momentum** $p(k):=\hbar k$ in $\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-1}$,
where $c=2{,}99792458\times10^{8}\ \mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-1}$ and
$\hbar=h/(2\pi)>0$ in $\mathrm J\,\mathrm s$ have the SI values of
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]] clause (c). Ordinary frequency is
$\nu(k)=\omega(k)/(2\pi)$ in hertz. These are separate quantum-radiation model
assignments: they are neither consequences of classical Maxwell theory nor
consequences of the special-relativistic framework, and no Lorentz
transformation law for the mode label $k$, for $\omega(k)$ or for the
polarisation pair is adopted or claimed; the extension does not assert Galilean
covariance of the radiation sector, and it does not identify the massless
Lorentz representations of the photon with the representations of the spatial
rotation group used in P6.

**(iv) Free-field observables.** The model assigns the total free-field energy
observable $H_f=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}T_{n}$ with $\varepsilon(k)=\hbar c|k|$ and
$T_{n}\psi=\varepsilon_{n}\psi$, read in joules, the total number observable $N$
read in the dimensionless unit $1$ of counted quanta, and the total momentum
components $\bigoplus_n\bigl(\sum_{i=1}^{n}\hbar k_{j,i}\bigr)$, read in
$\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-1}$; their operator domains and
self-adjointness are the mathematics of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-transverse-continuum-free-fock-hamiltonian]]
and [[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-number-operator-domain]], read physically
in [[def-nrqm-photons-framework-radiation-sector-and-quantum-assignments]].

**(v) Counting, detection and light-matter coupling are not supplied.** Photon
number and energy *statistics* require a declared detector model in the sense
of P2 and P7, which this postulate does not supply; a prescribed classical
electromagnetic field does not by itself yield photon counting or vacuum
spontaneous emission. No light-matter Hamiltonian, no dipole coupling, no
emission or absorption process and no recoil model is asserted here; the
absorption/stimulated-emission branch with a finite-level dipole coupling and
the quantised-mode emission construction are separate model assumptions for
the later pair on light-matter and spectral transitions. The relation of a
laboratory field, polariser or detector to this model is a tested
identification with uncertainty under P7, not a consequence of the postulate.

**(vi) Scope of the framework.** The radiation extension is deliberately
non-relativistic in its matter sector: it adds external free radiation modes to
the fixed-particle-number massive matter core without changing P5. Relativistic
matter, antiparticles, pair creation, covariant local field dynamics and full
quantum electrodynamics are not contained in this extension and are not
disguised as solved core prerequisites; they require a named field-theory
destination. No position wave function of the photon satisfying the massive
Schrödinger equation is introduced.

**(vii) Status.** Clauses (i)-(vi) are adopted assumptions of the model. They
are motivated by the sources cited above -- the transverse two-state
description of polarisation with transmitted fraction $\cos^{2}\theta$, the
single-mode oscillator quantisation with photon energy increment $\hbar\omega$,
and the field-operator expansion of free modes -- but motivation is not
deduction. No empirical claim, no measured value and no claim that any
laboratory field, polariser or detector is exactly described by the model is
made by this item.

## Status and scope

- **Adopted, not derived.** Neither the two-dimensional transverse
  polarisation space, nor the bosonic Fock assignment, nor the relations
  $\omega=c|k|$, $E=\hbar\omega$ and $p=\hbar k$ follow from P1-P7. They are the
  additional model content of this page, adopted only by the items that cite
  this postulate.
- **Relation to the massive model.** The extension is not obtained by any
  limit of the massive free Schrödinger model; the framework's own
  counterexample [[cex-nrqm-framework-zero-mass-has-no-self-adjoint-limit]]
  refutes that inference on explicit data, and the separate quantum-radiation
  assignments are declared directly. The polarisation internal space is a
  finite-state model, not a position representation of a photon.
- **Empirical qualifications.** The statistics choice, the transverse
  polarisation count, and the frequency-energy-momentum assignments are
  empirical model choices with uncertainties carried by their laboratory
  identifications. No experiment, count, efficiency or calibration is recorded
  or assumed by this postulate; comparisons with data belong to the
  preparation-and-apparatus discipline of P7.
items.physical_scope: The adopted radiation extension of the non-relativistic quantum framework: a fixed propagation-mode one-photon polarisation model with a two-dimensional transverse internal space, and a quantised free transverse radiation sector with bosonic Fock space and the mode assignments omega=c|k|, photon energy E=hbar*omega and photon momentum p=hbar*k in a declared inertial laboratory chart. The extension is an explicitly adopted model assumption; it is not derived from classical Maxwell theory, from special relativity, or from the massive-particle model by a mass-to-zero limit, and no Lorentz transformation law for the mode labels and no Galilean covariance of the radiation sector are claimed. Detection, coupling to matter and spontaneous emission are not supplied by this postulate.

items.statement:
## Definition

**(a) Adopted readings.** Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the
observable and probability postulate P2 and the identical-particle and spin
postulate P6 ([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]]) and the radiation
extension postulate
[[post-nrqm-photons-radiation-extension-and-transverse-mode-assignment]] in
its clauses (i)-(iv), read in the state vocabulary of
[[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]], the observable vocabulary of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]], the sector
vocabulary of
[[def-nrqm-identical-particles-framework-species-sectors-and-preparations]]
and the units of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. Assume the
Axioms of Countable Choice and of Choice, the choice hypotheses of the cited
Fock space mathematics ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

**(b) Radiation one-particle space and sectors.** The **transverse one-particle
space** of the radiation sector is
$$\mathfrak h:=\Bigl\{f\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{3}):\ k\cdot f(k)=0\ \text{for almost every }k\Bigr\}$$
with the restricted $L^{2}$ inner product, a separable complex Hilbert space
([[def-hilbert-space]]); its elements are read as **one-photon wave-packet
vectors**. For $n\ge1$ the **$n$-photon sector** is
$\mathfrak H_{n}^{+}=\operatorname{ran}P_{+}^{(n)}\subseteq\mathfrak h^{\otimes n}$
and the **radiation state space** is the bosonic Fock space
$F(\mathfrak h)=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}\mathfrak H_{n}^{+}$, whose sector projections
are $\Pi_n$ and whose vacuum is $\Omega=\iota_0(1)$
([[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-hilbert-direct-sum-construction]],
[[lem-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-fock-sector-projections]]). A **declared
radiation preparation** is a state $\rho\in D(F(\mathfrak h))$ in the sense of
[[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]]; a **declared one-photon
preparation** is a preparation whose state is supported in the one-photon
sector, and for a unit $f\in\mathfrak h$ the ray of $\iota_{1}(f)$ is the
one-photon preparation **of wave-packet vector $f$**.

**(c) Modes.** A **mode** of the radiation sector is a nonzero class
$\varphi\in\mathfrak h$ considered up to phase, equivalently the rank-one
orthogonal projection onto $\mathbb C\varphi$; a **declared mode family** is a
finite or countable orthonormal family $(\varphi_{j})$ of $\mathfrak h$
([[def-orthonormal-family-complete-orthonormal-system-and-hilbert-basis]]). For
a unit mode vector $\varphi$ and $z\in\mathbb C$ the vector
$$U_\varphi\psi_z,\qquad \psi_z=e^{-|z|^{2}/2}\sum_{n\in\mathbb N}\frac{z^{n}}{\sqrt{n!}}e_n,$$
is the **mode-coherent preparation vector of label $z$**, and $U_\varphi e_n$
is the **$n$-quanta mode vector**; these are the readings of the transferred
vectors of [[lem-nrqm-photons-fixed-mode-number-isometry]]. A mode vector is a
normalisable wave packet; the sharp-mode label $k$ of the propagation-mode
idealisation is a spectral parameter and is not a state of $\mathfrak h$
([[lem-nrqm-photons-transverse-restricted-momentum-and-energy-multipliers]]
clause (c)).

**(d) Assigned observables.** The framework assigns to the radiation sector:

1. the **total number observable** $(N,1)$, the self-adjoint number operator of
   [[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-number-operator-domain]], with domain
   $D(N)=\{\psi:\sum_nn^{2}\|\psi_n\|^{2}<\infty\}$ and read in the
   dimensionless unit $1$ of counted quanta;
2. the **free-field energy observable** $(H_f,\mathrm J)$, the operator
   $H_f=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}T_{n}$ with $\varepsilon(k)=\hbar c|k|$ and
   $T_{n}\psi=\varepsilon_{n}\psi$, of
   [[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-transverse-continuum-free-fock-hamiltonian]],
   read in joules; its one-particle restriction is the energy multiplier
   $M_{\hbar c|k|}^{\mathfrak h}$ of
   [[lem-nrqm-photons-transverse-restricted-momentum-and-energy-multipliers]];
3. for $j\in\{1,2,3\}$ the **one-photon momentum component**
   $(M_{\hbar k_{j}}^{\mathfrak h},\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-1})$ of
   [[lem-nrqm-photons-transverse-restricted-momentum-and-energy-multipliers]],
   read in $\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-1}$; this page assigns the
   momentum components on the one-photon sector and no second-quantised
   total-momentum operator is needed by any statement of this page.

**(e) Reading of the mode assignments.** In the declared inertial chart the
assignments $\omega(k)=c|k|$ in $\mathrm s^{-1}$, $E(k)=\hbar\omega(k)$ in
$\mathrm J$ and $p(k)=\hbar k$ in $\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-1}$ of
clause (iii) of the radiation postulate are read through the spectral measures
of clause (d): for a one-photon preparation of unit wave-packet vector
$f\in D(\varepsilon_{\mathfrak h})$, the **assigned frequency**, **energy** and
**momentum component** laws are the push-forwards of the measure
$\|f(k)\|_{\mathbb C^{3}}^{2}\,d^{3}k$ under $k\mapsto c|k|$,
$k\mapsto\hbar c|k|$ and $k\mapsto\hbar k_{j}$; these laws and their means are proved on this page. Sharp
frequency, sharp energy and sharp momentum-component states are not vectors of
$\mathfrak h$; every unit one-photon vector has strictly positive variance in
each of these quantities (clause (d) of
[[lem-nrqm-photons-transverse-restricted-momentum-and-energy-multipliers]]),
so the phrase "photon of energy $\hbar\omega$" names a spectral assignment of
the model, not a normalisable state with an exact energy.

**(f) Scope.** Clauses (b)-(e) fix the sector assignment and the units. They
assert no detector model, no sampling model, no dynamics, no interaction with
matter, no spontaneous emission and no empirical result; the counting and detection vocabulary is fixed separately on this page. The
identification of a laboratory radiation field with a preparation of
$F(\mathfrak h)$ is a tested identification with uncertainty under P7, and no
Lorentz transformation law for modes or their labels is adopted or claimed.

items.title: The fixed-mode polarisation model of the framework
items.statement:
## Definition

**(a) Adopted readings.** Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the
observable and probability postulate P2, the ideal conditional-measurement
postulate P3, the preparation and apparatus discipline P7
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-ideal-conditional-measurement]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]) and the radiation
extension postulate
[[post-nrqm-photons-radiation-extension-and-transverse-mode-assignment]] in
its clause (i). Read the state vocabulary in
[[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]], the observable vocabulary
in [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]], the
measurement vocabulary in
[[def-nrqm-measurement-framework-declared-measurements-and-instruments]], and
the units of angles in [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]: angles and
phases are dimensionless under the radian convention. Assume the Axiom of
Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice, the choice hypotheses of the cited
readings ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

**(b) Declared fixed-mode data.** A **declared fixed-mode polarisation model**
consists of:

1. a nonzero **propagation label** $k_{0}\in\mathbb R^{3}\setminus\{0\}$, read
   in $\mathrm m^{-1}$ in a declared inertial chart, which is a parameter of the
   model and not a state;
2. a declared **transverse frame**, that is an orthonormal pair $(v_{1},v_{2})$
   in the euclidean space $\mathbb C^{3}$ with $\langle v_{i},v_{j}\rangle=\delta_{ij}$
   and $k_{0}\cdot v_{1}=k_{0}\cdot v_{2}=0$;
3. the **polarisation space** $V:=\mathbb Cv_{1}\oplus\mathbb Cv_{2}$ with the
   restricted Hermitian inner product and the orthonormal basis
   $(e_{1},e_{2}):=(v_{1},v_{2})$.

The model's **state space** is $D(V)$, the set of density operators of $V$; the
**pure preparations** of the model are the unit rays $[\psi]$ of $V$, that is
the preparations assigned the pure state $\widehat\rho(\psi)$ of
[[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]], and a **mixed
preparation** is a statistical mixture of preparations in the sense of P1. The
map $\theta\mapsto\psi_{\theta}:=\cos\theta\,e_{1}+\sin\theta\,e_{2}$ assigns
to each angle $\theta\in\mathbb R$ a distinguished pure preparation, the
**linear polarisation preparation at angle $\theta$** in the declared
transverse frame.

**(c) Declared polarisation analyser.** For each angle $\theta\in\mathbb R$ the
**declared polarisation analyser at angle $\theta$** is the declared ideal
sharp measurement of clause (a) of
[[def-nrqm-measurement-framework-declared-measurements-and-instruments]] with
two outcomes labelled $+1$ and $-1$ and outcome structure
$$(P_{\theta},\,P_{\theta}^{\perp}),\qquad P_{\theta}x=\langle x,e_{\theta}\rangle e_{\theta},\quad e_{\theta}:=\cos\theta\,e_{1}+\sin\theta\,e_{2},\qquad P_{\theta}^{\perp}:=I-P_{\theta},$$
whose projections $P_{\theta},P_{\theta}^{\perp}$ are those of
[[lem-nrqm-photons-analyzer-projections-and-overlaps]]. The **outcome law** of
the analyser in a preparation $\rho$ is the reading of P2 for the projections
of the outcome structure, and the labels are dimensionless with the reading
"$+1$: transmitted", "$-1$: blocked". Where a conditional post-measurement
state is used, it is the Lueders update of clause (b) of
[[def-nrqm-measurement-framework-declared-measurements-and-instruments]]; the
framework does not assert that a laboratory absorber leaves an outgoing
one-photon polarisation state, and the absorption outcome is used only through
its discarded-outcome law unless a separate instrument is declared (clause (v)
of P3).

**(d) Frame and label reading.** Replacing the declared transverse frame
$(v_{1},v_{2})$ by another orthonormal pair changes the numerical angle
assigned to a given preparation, but the family $\{P_{\theta}\}_{\theta}$ of
analyser projections and the outcome law of any declared analyser-preparation
pair are unchanged as a family read against the declared frame; the model's
outcome numbers depend on the pair up to the rotated labelling of angles. The
value of $|k_{0}|$ enters no polarisation outcome of this model: by clause (i)
of the radiation postulate it enters the frequency and energy assignments
$\omega_{0}=c|k_{0}|$ and $E_{0}=\hbar\omega_{0}$ of the mode, which are read on the radiation sector of the model, not on the two-dimensional polarisation factor.

**(e) Scope.** The model is an idealisation of a transverse propagation mode
with a definite mode label. It is a finite-dimensional internal-factor model
in the sense of P1 and P6: its state space is $D(V)$, its preparations are
rays, and its analyser is a declared ideal sharp measurement. It contains no
position observable, no momentum observable, no spatial wave function and no
localisation claim, and it is not the massive one-particle model of P5 with
$m=0$ and is not obtained from that model by a mass-to-zero limit; no such
limit is used or claimed. The mode label $k_{0}$ is not a
normalisable state of any sector of the framework, and a plane wave is not
introduced as a state. Whether a laboratory polariser and source realize this
declared model, with what efficiency, loss and background, is a tested
identification with uncertainty under P7, not a consequence of this
definition.

**(f) Status.** Clauses (a)-(e) fix the model data, its outcome vocabulary and
its scope; they add no assumption beyond the cited postulates and the cited
finite-dimensional mathematics. The mathematical properties of the projections
are the content of
[[lem-nrqm-photons-analyzer-projections-and-overlaps]]; the conditional outcome law of the declared analyser is proved on this page. No empirical claim is made here.
items.physical_scope: The declared fixed propagation-mode polarisation model of the framework: a nonzero wavevector label, a declared orthonormal pair spanning the transverse plane, the two-dimensional complex polarisation space with its unit rays as idealised one-photon polarisation preparations, and the two-outcome polarisation analyser family with the Born outcome law of P2 and the Lueders reading of P3 where used. The model is an adopted idealisation of a transverse mode with a definite propagation label; it is not a spatial wave function, has no position or momentum observable, is not the massless limit of the massive model, and asserts no localisation, no detector response, no loss, no efficiency and no empirical result.

items.title: The analyser outcome law of the fixed-mode polarisation model: Born probabilities and the Malus ratio
items.statement:
## Statement

Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the observable and probability
postulate P2 and the ideal conditional-measurement postulate P3
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-ideal-conditional-measurement]]), the radiation
extension postulate clause (i)
([[post-nrqm-photons-radiation-extension-and-transverse-mode-assignment]]) and
the declared fixed-mode polarisation model
[[def-nrqm-photons-framework-fixed-mode-polarization-model]], in the state
vocabulary of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]] and the
observable and measurement vocabularies of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] and
[[def-nrqm-measurement-framework-declared-measurements-and-instruments]].
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice, the choice
hypotheses of the cited spectral and measurement mathematics
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Fix angles
$\varphi,\theta,\theta'\in\mathbb R$ and write
$\psi_{\varphi}=\cos\varphi\,e_{1}+\sin\varphi\,e_{2}$ and
$P_{\theta}$ for the analyser projections of the model. Then:

(a) the declared polarisation analyser at angle $\theta$ is a declared ideal
sharp measurement with outcome structure $(P_{\theta},P_{\theta}^{\perp})$, the
outcome labels $+1$ and $-1$ naming the first and second projection, in
the sense of clause (a) of
[[def-nrqm-measurement-framework-declared-measurements-and-instruments]]:
$P_{\theta}$ and $P_{\theta}^{\perp}$ are bounded orthogonal projections with
$P_{\theta}P_{\theta}^{\perp}=0$ and $P_{\theta}+P_{\theta}^{\perp}=I$;

(b) the spectral projection-valued measure $E$ of the bounded self-adjoint
operator $P_{\theta}$ (assigned with unit $1$; its values on the two outcomes
are $1$ and $0$, while the analyser labels are $+1$ and $-1$) satisfies
$$E(\{1\})=P_{\theta},\qquad E(\{0\})=P_{\theta}^{\perp},\qquad E(\mathbb R\setminus\{0,1\})=0,$$
consequently the outcome law of the assigned sharp quantity $P_{\theta}$ in a
preparation $\rho\in D(V)$ is
$$p_{+1}(\rho)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho P_{\theta}),\qquad p_{-1}(\rho)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho P_{\theta}^{\perp})=1-p_{+1}(\rho),$$
which is exactly the law of the declared analyser;

(c) for the linear-polarisation preparation $\psi_{\varphi}$ and a general
pure preparation with unit vector $\psi=\alpha e_{1}+\beta e_{2}$,
$$p_{+1}(\psi_{\varphi})=\cos^{2}(\theta-\varphi),\qquad p_{-1}(\psi_{\varphi})=\sin^{2}(\theta-\varphi),\qquad p_{+1}(\psi)=|\alpha\cos\theta+\beta\sin\theta|^{2};$$
for a statistical mixture $\rho=\sum_{n}w_{n}\rho_{n}$ of preparations the law
is affine, $p_{+1}(\rho)=\sum_{n}w_{n}p_{+1}(\rho_{n})$;

(d) the law is invariant under the phase of the preparation and under the
phase of the analysed direction: $p_{+1}$ depends only on the rays
$[\psi_{\varphi}]$ and $[e_{\theta}]$, is $2\pi$-periodic in each argument, and
satisfies $p_{+1}(\theta,\varphi)=p_{+1}(\theta-\varphi,0)$;

(e) if $p_{+1}(\rho)>0$, the conditional state after the outcome $+1$ of the
analyser is $\rho_{+1}=P_{\theta}\rho P_{\theta}/p_{+1}(\rho)$; for the pure
preparation $[\psi_{\varphi}]$ with $\cos(\theta-\varphi)\ne0$ it is the pure
state of the analysed ray $[e_{\theta}]$, and a second analyser at angle
$\theta'$ then gives the conditional probability
$\cos^{2}(\theta'-\theta)$ for the outcome $+1$. If the outcome is discarded,
the state is $\Phi(\rho)=P_{\theta}\rho P_{\theta}+P_{\theta}^{\perp}\rho P_{\theta}^{\perp}$;

(f) the assertions (a)-(e) are conditional consequences of P1, P2, P3 and the
adopted model. They assert no dynamics, no laboratory polariser, no detector
efficiency, no loss, no sampling model and no empirical result; in particular
the fraction $\cos^{2}(\theta-\varphi)$ is a model probability of the declared
ideal analyser, not a measured count.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** the postulates P1, P2, P3 and the declared fixed-mode model with polarisation space $V$, orthonormal basis $(e_{1},e_{2})$, rays $[\psi_{\varphi}]$ and analyser projections $P_{\theta},P_{\theta}^{\perp}$, together with the cited spectral and measurement mathematics.

[F1] **Projection pair.** $P_{\theta}$ and $P_{\theta}^{\perp}$ are orthogonal projections on $V$ with $P_{\theta}P_{\theta}=P_{\theta}=P_{\theta}^{*}$, $P_{\theta}+P_{\theta}^{\perp}=I$, $P_{\theta}P_{\theta}^{\perp}=P_{\theta}^{\perp}P_{\theta}=0$, $\|P_{\theta}\|=1$, and their ranges are $\mathbb Ce_{\theta}$ and $\mathbb Ce_{\theta}^{\perp}$: $\ker(P_{\theta}-I)=\mathbb Ce_{\theta}$, $\ker P_{\theta}=\mathbb Ce_{\theta}^{\perp}$ ([[lem-nrqm-photons-analyzer-projections-and-overlaps]] clauses (a),(d), [[def-hilbert-orthogonal-projection]]).

[F2] **Analyser law.** For the declared analyser the outcome law of clause (ii) of P2 is $\rho\mapsto\operatorname{tr}(\rho E_{\theta}(\cdot))$ for the spectral measure of the assigned observable; a declared ideal sharp measurement has mutually orthogonal projections with strong sum $I$, outcome probabilities $\operatorname{tr}(\rho P_{a})$ and Lueders update of clause (b) of the measurement definition ([[def-nrqm-measurement-framework-declared-measurements-and-instruments]] clauses (a),(b), [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (b)).

[F3] **Spectral atoms.** For a self-adjoint operator $A$ with spectral measure $E$, the projection $E(\{\lambda\})$ is the orthogonal projection onto $\ker(A-\lambda)$; hence at an eigenvalue $\lambda$ with eigenspace $\mathbb C u$, $u$ unit, one has $E(\{\lambda\})=T_{u,u}$ and $\operatorname{tr}(\rho E(\{\lambda\}))=\langle u,\rho u\rangle$ ([[lem-nrqm-observables-spectral-measure-atoms-and-eigenvalues]] clause (a)).

[F4] **Overlaps.** For all real $\varphi,\theta$: $\langle e_{\theta},\psi_{\varphi}\rangle=\cos(\theta-\varphi)$ and $\|P_{\theta}\psi_{\varphi}\|^{2}=\langle\psi_{\varphi},P_{\theta}\psi_{\varphi}\rangle=\cos^{2}(\theta-\varphi)$; moreover $P_{\theta}(z\psi)=zP_{\theta}\psi$ for all $z\in\mathbb C$ ([[lem-nrqm-photons-analyzer-projections-and-overlaps]] clauses (b),(c)).

[F5] **Affinity and updates.** The outcome law of an assigned sharp observable is affine in the preparation: $\mu^{A}_{\sum_{n}w_{n}\rho_{n}}=\sum_{n}w_{n}\mu^{A}_{\rho_{n}}$; the selective Lueders update of a declared ideal sharp measurement with outcome projection $P_{a}$ and $p_{a}=\operatorname{tr}(\rho P_{a})>0$ is $\rho_{a}=P_{a}\rho P_{a}/p_{a}$, and the discarded-outcome state is $\Phi(\rho)=\sum_{a}P_{a}\rho P_{a}$ ([[lem-nrqm-observables-outcome-law-affinity-and-trace-norm-continuity]], [[lem-nrqm-measurement-selective-luders-update]], [[lem-nrqm-measurement-nonselective-luders-map]], [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]]).

## Proof

1.1 [The analyser is a declared ideal sharp measurement] By [F1] the two projections of the analyser are bounded, orthogonal and mutually orthogonal with $P_{\theta}+P_{\theta}^{\perp}=I$; therefore the pair $(P_{\theta},P_{\theta}^{\perp})$ is a declared ideal sharp measurement in the sense of clause (a) of the measurement definition, with outcome labels $+1$ and $-1$. This is (a). [F1, F2, algebra]

1.2 [Spectral law] The operator $P_{\theta}$ is bounded and self-adjoint by [F1], so it has a spectral projection-valued measure $E$ ([[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (b)). Its eigenvalues are $1$ and $0$, with eigenspaces $\mathbb Ce_{\theta}$ and $\mathbb Ce_{\theta}^{\perp}$ by [F1]; by [F3], $E(\{1\})$ is the orthogonal projection onto $\mathbb Ce_{\theta}$, that is $P_{\theta}$, and $E(\{0\})$ is the orthogonal projection onto $\mathbb Ce_{\theta}^{\perp}$, that is $P_{\theta}^{\perp}=I-P_{\theta}$. Since $P_{\theta}$ is a projection one has $P_{\theta}^2=P_{\theta}$, so for $\lambda\notin\{0,1\}$ the bounded operator $\frac{1}{1-\lambda}P_{\theta}-\frac{1}{\lambda}(I-P_{\theta})$ is a two-sided inverse of $P_{\theta}-\lambda I$ (multiplying out gives $P_{\theta}+(I-P_{\theta})=I$), hence the spectrum is contained in $\{0,1\}$ ([[def-resolvent-and-spectrum-of-a-closed-unbounded-operator]], [[def-hilbert-orthogonal-projection]]); therefore $E(\mathbb R\setminus\{0,1\})=E(\mathbb R\setminus\sigma(P_{\theta}))=0$ by [[lem-nrqm-observables-spectral-support-and-outcome-law]] clause (a). For any preparation $\rho$ the outcome law of the assigned quantity $P_{\theta}$ at the value $1$ is $\operatorname{tr}(\rho E(\{1\}))=\operatorname{tr}(\rho P_{\theta})$ by [F2]; at the value $-1$ the projection is $E(\{0\})=P_{\theta}^{\perp}$, and the two weights sum to $\operatorname{tr}(\rho I)=1$. This is (b). [F1, F2, F3, algebra]

1.3 [Pure preparations] Let $\psi=\alpha e_{1}+\beta e_{2}$ be a unit vector. Since $E(\{1\})=P_{\theta}$, the probability is $\|P_{\theta}\psi\|^{2}=\langle\psi,P_{\theta}\psi\rangle=|\langle\psi,e_{\theta}\rangle|^{2}=|\alpha\cos\theta+\beta\sin\theta|^{2}$; for $\psi=\psi_{\varphi}$ this equals $\cos^{2}(\theta-\varphi)$ by [F4], and then $p_{-1}=1-p_{+1}=\sin^{2}(\theta-\varphi)$. [F1, F3, F4, algebra]

1.4 [Mixtures and phases] If $\rho=\sum_{n}w_{n}\rho_{n}$ is a statistical mixture, [F5] gives $p_{+1}(\rho)=\sum_{n}w_{n}\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{n}P_{\theta})=\sum_{n}w_{n}p_{+1}(\rho_{n})$. The number $|\langle z\psi,e_{\theta}\rangle|^{2}/\|z\psi\|^{2}=|\langle\psi,e_{\theta}\rangle|^{2}$ for $z\ne0$ is unchanged by scaling the representative, so the law depends only on the rays; the identities $P_{\theta+2\pi}=P_{\theta}$ and $P_{\theta+\pi}=P_{\theta}$ of [F4] give the stated periodicities, and $p_{+1}(\theta,\varphi)=\cos^{2}(\theta-\varphi)=p_{+1}(\theta-\varphi,0)$. This proves (c) and (d). [F4, F5, algebra]

2.1 [Conditional and discarded states] Let $\rho$ be a preparation with $p_{+1}(\rho)>0$. By [F5] the conditional state after the outcome $+1$ is $\rho_{+1}=P_{\theta}\rho P_{\theta}/p_{+1}(\rho)$. For the pure preparation of $\psi_{\varphi}$ with $\cos(\theta-\varphi)\ne0$ one has $P_{\theta}\psi_{\varphi}=\langle\psi_{\varphi},e_{\theta}\rangle e_{\theta}=\cos(\theta-\varphi)e_{\theta}$ by [F4]; hence $P_{\theta}\rho P_{\theta}=|\cos(\theta-\varphi)|^{2}T_{e_{\theta},e_{\theta}}$ and $\rho_{+1}=T_{e_{\theta},e_{\theta}}$, the pure state of the ray $[e_{\theta}]$ ([[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]]). Applying the pure-preparation formula of step 1.3 to the preparation $[e_{\theta}]$ at analyser angle $\theta'$ gives conditional probability $|\langle e_{\theta},e_{\theta'}\rangle|^{2}=\cos^{2}(\theta'-\theta)$ by [F4]. The discarded-outcome state is $\Phi(\rho)=P_{\theta}\rho P_{\theta}+P_{\theta}^{\perp}\rho P_{\theta}^{\perp}$ by [F5]. This proves (e). [F4, F5, step 1.3, algebra]

3.1 [Assembly and scope] Steps 1.1 and 1.2 prove (a) and (b), steps 1.3 and 1.4 prove (c) and (d), and step 2.1 proves (e). All assertions are conditional on P1, P2, P3 and the adopted model; no laboratory apparatus, no sampling model and no measured number occurs in the argument, which is (f). [step 1.1, step 1.2, step 1.3, step 1.4, step 2.1] ∎

## Remarks

- **The same number classically.** The number $\cos^{2}(\theta-\varphi)$ is also
  the intensity ratio of the declared classical transverse-field model of
  [[ex-nrqm-photons-malus-and-jones-analyzer-ratios]]; the comparison shows
  that this ratio alone does not distinguish the two declared models.
- **Absorption.** For a laboratory absorber the "blocked" outcome of the
  declared analyser is used only through its discarded-outcome law: clause (v)
  of P3 asserts no post-absorption one-photon state, and no such state is used
  here.
items.physical_scope: The conditional outcome law of the declared polarisation analyser of the fixed propagation-mode model: the analyser is a declared ideal sharp measurement with projections P_theta and P_theta-perp, its Born law in a pure linear-polarisation preparation is cos^2(theta-phi) and sin^2(theta-phi), the law is affine over statistical mixtures and invariant under the phases of the preparation, the conditional post-passage state is the analysed polarisation ray, and a second ideal analyser gives the relative cos^2 law. The result is conditional on P1, P2, P3 and the adopted model; no laboratory polariser is identified with the declared ideal analyser and no empirical result is asserted.
