items.title: Number, energy and momentum laws of a one-photon preparation
items.statement:
## Statement

Adopt the state and composition postulate P1 and the observable and
probability postulate P2 ([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]]), the radiation extension
postulate
([[post-nrqm-photons-radiation-extension-and-transverse-mode-assignment]]) and
the radiation sector definition
[[def-nrqm-photons-framework-radiation-sector-and-quantum-assignments]], in
the state vocabulary of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]] and
the observable vocabulary of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]. Assume the
Axioms of Countable Choice and of Choice, the choice hypotheses of the cited
operator and spectral items ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]).
Let $f\in\mathfrak h$ be a unit one-photon wave-packet vector with
$f\in D(\varepsilon_{\mathfrak h})$, $\varepsilon(k)=\hbar c|k|$, and let
$\rho_{f}$ be the one-photon preparation of the ray of $\iota_{1}(f)$. Then:

(a) *number law*: the outcome law of the assigned total-number observable
$(N,1)$ in $\rho_{f}$ is $\mu^{N}_{\rho_{f}}(B)=\mathbf 1_{B}(1)$ for every
Borel set $B\subseteq\mathbb R$: the number readout of the one-photon
preparation is one with probability one;

(b) *energy law*: the outcome law of the assigned free-field energy observable
$(H_f,\mathrm J)$ in $\rho_{f}$ is the push-forward of the finite measure
$\|f(k)\|_{\mathbb C^{3}}^{2}\,d^{3}k$ under $k\mapsto\hbar c|k|$:
$$\mu^{H_f}_{\rho_{f}}(B)=\int_{\varepsilon^{-1}(B)}\|f(k)\|_{\mathbb C^{3}}^{2}\,d^{3}k\qquad(B\subseteq\mathbb R\ \text{Borel}),$$
and the mean is the finite number
$$\langle H_f\rangle_{\rho_{f}}=\langle\varepsilon_{\mathfrak h}f,f\rangle=\hbar c\int_{\mathbb R^{3}}|k|\,\|f(k)\|_{\mathbb C^{3}}^{2}\,d^{3}k<\infty;$$

(c) *momentum readouts*: for $j\in\{1,2,3\}$ the one-photon momentum-component
readout of clause (d)(3) of
[[def-nrqm-photons-framework-radiation-sector-and-quantum-assignments]] has,
in the identification of the one-photon sector with $\mathfrak h$ by
$\iota_{1}$, the outcome law
$$\mu^{P_{j}}_{\rho_{f}}(B)=\int_{\{k:\hbar k_{j}\in B\}}\|f(k)\|_{\mathbb C^{3}}^{2}\,d^{3}k\qquad(B\subseteq\mathbb R\ \text{Borel}),$$
the push-forward of $\|f\|^{2}\,d^{3}k$ under $k\mapsto\hbar k_{j}$, with mean
$\hbar\int k_{j}\|f(k)\|^{2}\,d^{3}k$ whenever the latter integral is finite;

(d) *no sharp frequency, energy or momentum*: for every unit vector
$f\in\mathfrak h$ in the relevant domain, the variance of the energy law of
(b) and the variance of each momentum-component law of (c) are strictly
positive; consequently the mode assignment "photon energy $E=\hbar\omega$,
$\omega=c|k|$" is a spectral assignment of the model and never an exact value
of a normalisable one-photon state;

(e) all assertions are conditional on P1, P2 and the adopted radiation model;
they record no detector model, no sampling model, no measured count and no
empirical claim.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** the postulates P1, P2 and the adopted radiation model with transverse space $\mathfrak h$, sectors $\mathfrak H_{n}^{+}$, number operator $N$, free-field energy $H_f$ with $\varepsilon(k)=\hbar c|k|$, one-photon momentum readouts $M_{\hbar k_{j}}^{\mathfrak h}$, and a unit $f\in\mathfrak h$.

[F1] **Sector structure.** $\Pi_{n}$ is the orthogonal projection of $F(\mathfrak h)$ onto the closed subspace $\iota_{n}(\mathfrak H_{n}^{+})$, the ranges are pairwise orthogonal, $\sum_{n}\Pi_{n}=I$ in the strong operator topology, and $\|\psi\|^{2}=\sum_{n}\|\Pi_{n}\psi\|^{2}$ ([[lem-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-fock-sector-projections]] clauses (a)-(c)).

[F2] **Number operator.** $N$ is self-adjoint with $D(N)=\{\psi:\sum_{n}n^{2}\|\psi_{n}\|^{2}<\infty\}$, $N\iota_{n}(u)=n\,\iota_{n}(u)$ for every $u\in\mathfrak H_{n}^{+}$, and $\sigma(N)=\mathbb N$ ([[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-number-operator-domain]] clauses (a),(b)).

[F3] **Spectral atoms.** For a self-adjoint operator $A$ with spectral measure $E_A$, $E_A(\{\lambda\})$ is the orthogonal projection onto the eigenspace $\ker(A-\lambda)$; for a unit eigenvector $u$ at $\lambda$ and a pure state $\rho=T_{u,u}$ one has $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\{\lambda\})=1$ ([[lem-nrqm-observables-spectral-measure-atoms-and-eigenvalues]] clauses (a),(b)).

[F4] **Free-field energy.** $H_f=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}T_{n}$ with $T_{n}$ self-adjoint on $\operatorname{ran}P_{+}^{(n)}$, $T_{n}\psi=\varepsilon_{n}\psi$, is self-adjoint and positive with $D(H_f)=\{\psi:\sum_{n}\|T_{n}\psi_{n}\|^{2}<\infty\}$; its one-particle restriction is $\varepsilon_{\mathfrak h}$ ([[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-transverse-continuum-free-fock-hamiltonian]] clauses (a)-(c)).

[F5] **Direct-sum spectral measure.** If $(T_{n})$ are self-adjoint operators on the Hilbert spaces $\mathfrak H_{n}$ with spectral measures $E_{n}$, then $E(B):=\bigoplus_{n}E_{n}(B)$ is a projection-valued measure on $\bigoplus_{n}\mathfrak H_{n}$ and the spectral measure of the self-adjoint direct sum $\bigoplus_{n}T_{n}$: indeed $E$ is a regular projection-valued measure whose unbounded integral is $\bigoplus_{n}T_{n}$ with the direct-sum domain, and the spectral projection-valued measure of a self-adjoint operator is unique ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]], [[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-hilbert-direct-sum-construction]] clause (f), [[lem-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-fock-sector-projections]]).

[F6] **Restricted multipliers.** For $m\in\{\hbar c|k|,\hbar k_{j}\}$ the operator $M_{m}^{\mathfrak h}$ is self-adjoint on $\mathfrak h$ with spectral measure $E_{m}(B)=M_{\mathbf 1_{m^{-1}(B)}}|_{\mathfrak h}$, the law of a unit $g\in\mathfrak h$ is the push-forward of $\|g\|^{2}\,d^{3}k$ under $k\mapsto m(k)$, and $M_{m}^{\mathfrak h}$ has no eigenvalues; for unit $g\in D(M_{m}^{\mathfrak h})$ the variance is strictly positive ([[lem-nrqm-photons-transverse-restricted-momentum-and-energy-multipliers]] clauses (a)-(d)).

[F7] **Means and variances for pure states.** For a self-adjoint $A$ and a unit $u\in D(A)$ the mean of the outcome law in the pure state $T_{u,u}$ is $\langle Au,u\rangle$; the variance is $\|Au\|^{2}-\langle Au,u\rangle^{2}$ when $u\in D(A)$ ([[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (e)).

## Proof

1.1 [Number law] For $n\in\mathbb N$ the eigenspace of $N$ at $n$ is $\{\psi\in D(N):N\psi=n\psi\}$; comparing coordinates with the definition $(N\psi)_{m}=m\psi_{m}$, this eigenspace equals $\iota_{n}(\mathfrak H_{n}^{+})$, the closed subspace of vectors supported in coordinate $n$. Hence by [F3] the spectral projection is $E_{N}(\{n\})=\Pi_{n}$, and for the one-photon state $\rho_{f}=T_{\iota_{1}f,\iota_{1}f}$ we get $$\mu^{N}_{\rho_{f}}(\{n\})=\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{f}\Pi_{n})=\langle\Pi_{n}\iota_{1}f,\iota_{1}f\rangle=\delta_{n,1}$$ by [F1]; since the atoms cover $\mathbb N$ and the law is a measure, $\mu^{N}_{\rho_{f}}(B)=\mathbf 1_{B}(1)$ for every Borel set $B$. This proves (a). [F1, F2, F3, algebra]

1.2 [Energy law] By [F5] the spectral measure of $H_f$ is $E(B)=\bigoplus_{n}E_{T_{n}}(B)$, and on the one-photon sector $\iota_{1}\mathfrak H_{1}^{+}$ it acts as $\iota_{1}E_{T_{1}}(B)\iota_{1}^{-1}$; since $T_{1}=\varepsilon_{\mathfrak h}$ by [F4], the restriction is the spectral measure $E_{\varepsilon}(B)=M_{\mathbf 1_{\varepsilon^{-1}(B)}}|_{\mathfrak h}$ of [F6]. Therefore $$\mu^{H_f}_{\rho_{f}}(B)=\langle E(B)\iota_{1}f,\iota_{1}f\rangle=\langle E_{\varepsilon}(B)f,f\rangle=\int_{\varepsilon^{-1}(B)}\|f(k)\|^{2}\,d^{3}k,$$ which is the push-forward formula of (b). The mean exists and equals $\langle H_f\iota_{1}f,\iota_{1}f\rangle=\langle\varepsilon_{\mathfrak h}f,f\rangle=\hbar c\int|k|\|f\|^{2}<\infty$ by [F7], [F6] and $f\in D(\varepsilon_{\mathfrak h})$, the last integral being finite by definition of the domain and Hölder's inequality. [F4, F5, F6, F7, algebra]

1.3 [Momentum readouts] The same computation with $m=\hbar k_{j}$ in place of $\varepsilon$ and [F6] in place of [F4] gives $\mu^{P_{j}}_{\rho_{f}}(B)=\langle E_{m}(B)f,f\rangle=\int_{\{m\in B\}}\|f\|^{2}\,d^{3}k$, the push-forward under $k\mapsto\hbar k_{j}$; when $f\in D(M_{m}^{\mathfrak h})$ the mean is $\langle M_{m}^{\mathfrak h}f,f\rangle=\hbar\int k_{j}\|f\|^{2}\,d^{3}k$ by [F7], since the identification $\iota_{1}$ is isometric. This proves (c). [F6, F7, algebra]

2.1 [Strict positivity of the variances] By [F6] the multiplier $M_{\hbar c|k|}^{\mathfrak h}$ has no eigenvalues and every unit $f\in D(\varepsilon_{\mathfrak h})$ has strictly positive variance; together with step 1.2 and [F7] this gives the strict positivity of the energy variance. The same clause applied to $m=\hbar k_{j}$ gives strict positivity of each momentum-component variance whenever $f\in D(M_{\hbar k_{j}}^{\mathfrak h})$. Hence no unit vector of $\mathfrak h$ has a sharp value of energy or of any momentum component, and the assignment $E(k)=\hbar c|k|$, $p(k)=\hbar k$ of the radiation postulate is read only as a spectral assignment. This proves (d). [F6, step 1.2, step 1.3, algebra]

3.1 [Assembly and scope] Step 1.1 proves (a), steps 1.2 and 1.3 prove (b) and (c), and step 2.1 proves (d). No step introduces a detector, a sampling model, a measured count or an empirical premise, which is (e). [step 1.1, step 1.2, step 1.3, step 2.1] ∎

## Remarks

- **Reading the mean.** The energy mean $\hbar c\int|k|\|f\|^{2}$ is the
  first moment of the transverse momentum density weighted by $\hbar c$; it is
  a preparation mean of the model, not a measured energy, and it exists for
  every $f\in D(\varepsilon_{\mathfrak h})$ by the domain definition.
- **Why "photon energy $\hbar\omega$" remains meaningful.** For a model
  preparation concentrated near a wavevector $k_{0}$, the energy law is
  concentrated near $\hbar c|k_{0}|$ in the sense of the push-forward measure;
  the item claims no limit statement and no localisation, and the exact value
  is never attained by a normalisable vector.
items.physical_scope: The outcome laws of the assigned radiation observables in a declared one-photon preparation of the model: the number observable has the sharp value one; the free-field energy law is the push-forward of the transverse momentum density under k -> hbar*c*|k| with mean hbar*c*integral|k||f|^2 and strictly positive variance; and the one-photon momentum-component readouts are the push-forwards under k -> hbar*k_j with strictly positive variance. The result is conditional on P1, P2 and the adopted radiation model, records no detector, no sampling model and no measured number, and shows that no normalisable one-photon vector has sharp frequency, energy or momentum.

items.statement:
## Definition

**(a) Adopted readings.** Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the
observable and probability postulate P2, the ideal conditional-measurement
postulate P3 and the preparation and apparatus discipline P7
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-ideal-conditional-measurement]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]), the radiation extension
postulate
[[post-nrqm-photons-radiation-extension-and-transverse-mode-assignment]] and
the radiation sector definition
[[def-nrqm-photons-framework-radiation-sector-and-quantum-assignments]], in
the measurement vocabulary of
[[def-nrqm-measurement-framework-declared-measurements-and-instruments]].
Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and of Choice, the choice hypotheses of
the cited readings ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

**(b) Declared ideal total-number detector.** The **declared ideal
total-number detector** of the radiation sector is the declared ideal sharp
measurement with outcome set $\mathbb N$, outcome projection
$$P_{n}:=\Pi_{n}\qquad(n\in\mathbb N),$$
the sector projections of the Fock space $F(\mathfrak h)$; the family
$(\Pi_{n})$ consists of mutually orthogonal orthogonal projections with strong
sum $I$ ([[lem-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-fock-sector-projections]] clauses
(a),(b),(c)). Its **count law** in a declared radiation preparation $\rho$ is
the reading of clause (ii) of P2,
$$p_{n}(\rho)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho\Pi_{n}),\qquad \sum_{n\in\mathbb N}p_{n}(\rho)=1,$$
and its **number readout** is the assigned total-number observable $(N,1)$ of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-number-operator-domain]] read through the atom
law of P2. The conditional post-count state and the discarded-outcome state are
the Lueders updates of the measurement definition
([[lem-nrqm-measurement-selective-luders-update]],
[[lem-nrqm-measurement-nonselective-luders-map]]). The word "count" refers to
the quanta of the declared model; no laboratory counter, no absorption
process, no detection efficiency, no dark count, no dead time and no
background is declared here.

**(c) Declared ideal energy-window detector.** For a Borel set
$B\subseteq[0,\infty)$ read in joules the **declared ideal energy-window
detector of window $B$** is the declared ideal sharp measurement with outcome
structure
$$\bigl(E_{H_f}(B),\ I-E_{H_f}(B)\bigr),$$
where $E_{H_f}$ is the spectral projection-valued measure of the assigned
free-field energy observable $(H_f,\mathrm J)$; its **window law** in the
preparation $\rho$ is $p_{B}(\rho)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho E_{H_f}(B))$ and its
complement probability is $\operatorname{tr}(\rho(I-E_{H_f}(B)))$, the reading
of P2. A finite-resolution detector is described by such a window or by a
declared family of pairwise disjoint windows covering $[0,\infty)$; the
statement that a laboratory spectrometer realizes a declared window, with what
resolution and calibration, is an identification under P7.

**(d) Declared analyser detection.** The **declared polarisation-analyser
detection** of the fixed propagation mode is the analyser family
$\{P_{\theta},P_{\theta}^{\perp}\}$ of
[[def-nrqm-photons-framework-fixed-mode-polarization-model]], read as a
declared ideal sharp measurement of the polarisation factor; its law and its conditional update are proved on this page. It detects the polarisation alternative of the model and is not a photon counter.

**(e) Repetition requires a separate sampling model.** The declaration of a
detector gives the outcome law of a single declared measurement. A prediction
for repeated trials, a count rate, or any statistical comparison with data
requires in addition a declared preparation-and-apparatus model and a sampling
model in the sense of P7 -- for instance an identically-and-independently
repeated preparation with a declared number of trials -- which this page does
not supply. A single measurement outcome law is not a frequency and no
frequency is asserted.

**(f) Destructive detectors are outside the declared class.** A
photoabsorption detector that destroys the absorbed quantum, and any detector
whose post-outcome state of the radiation field is not the Lueders update,
requires its own declared instrument, that is its own outcome effects together
with its own conditional updates (clause (v) of P3, clause (d) of the
measurement definition). No such instrument is declared on this page, and the
"blocked" outcome of the analyser is used only through its discarded-outcome
law.

**(g) Status.** Clauses (b)-(d) fix vocabulary and read the cited postulates;
they add no physical assumption beyond P1-P3, P7 and the radiation model, and
they assert no detection mechanism, no response function and no empirical
result. In particular, the declaration of an ideal counting model is not a
claim that any physical device counts photons, and the energy-window model is
not a claim that any physical spectrometer measures exact energy.
items.physical_scope: The declared ideal detection models of the radiation sector: the ideal total-number counting model with the Fock sector projections as outcome structure and the Born law of P2, the ideal energy-window model with the spectral projections of the free-field energy, and the polarisation analyser of the fixed-mode model. The declaration fixes vocabulary only; it asserts no laboratory counter, no absorption instrument, no efficiency, no dark counts, no dead time, no background, no calibration and no sampling model, and repeated trials require a separately declared statistical model.

items.title: Number and energy statistics of a declared mode: number states, coherent states and the continuum thermal limitation
items.statement:
## Statement

Adopt the state and composition postulate P1 and the observable and
probability postulate P2 ([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]]), the radiation extension
postulate
([[post-nrqm-photons-radiation-extension-and-transverse-mode-assignment]]),
the radiation sector definition
[[def-nrqm-photons-framework-radiation-sector-and-quantum-assignments]] and
the declared ideal counting model
[[def-nrqm-photons-framework-ideal-counting-and-detection-model]]. Assume the
Axioms of Countable Choice and of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Fix a unit mode vector $\varphi\in\mathfrak h$, a
label $z\in\mathbb C$, and write $U:=U_\varphi$ for the fixed-mode isometry of
[[lem-nrqm-photons-fixed-mode-number-isometry]]. Then:

(a) for every $n\in\mathbb N$ the $n$-quanta mode vector $Ue_{n}=\varphi^{\otimes n}$
is a unit vector of the $n$-photon sector; the count law of the declared ideal
total-number detector in the preparation of its ray is
$p_{m}=\delta_{mn}$, and the number readout is $n$ with probability one;

(b) the count law of the mode-coherent preparation $U\psi_{z}$ of label $z$ is
the Poisson law
$$p_{n}=e^{-|z|^{2}}\frac{|z|^{2n}}{n!}\qquad(n\in\mathbb N),$$
with mean and variance
$$\sum_{n\in\mathbb N}n\,p_{n}=|z|^{2},\qquad \sum_{n\in\mathbb N}n^{2}p_{n}-\Bigl(\sum_{n\in\mathbb N}n\,p_{n}\Bigr)^{2}=|z|^{2};$$
in particular the mode-coherent preparation is not a number state unless
$z=0$;

(c) if $\varphi\in D(\varepsilon_{\mathfrak h})$, writing
$\bar\varepsilon:=\langle\varepsilon_{\mathfrak h}\varphi,\varphi\rangle=\hbar c\int|k|\,\|\varphi(k)\|^{2}\,d^{3}k$,
the energy means of the assigned free-field energy observable are
$$\langle H_f\rangle_{Ue_{n}}=n\,\bar\varepsilon,\qquad \langle H_f\rangle_{U\psi_{z}}=|z|^{2}\,\bar\varepsilon ;$$

(d) if moreover $\varphi\in D(\varepsilon_{\mathfrak h}^{2})$, writing
$\overline{\varepsilon^{2}}:=\langle\varepsilon_{\mathfrak h}^{2}\varphi,\varphi\rangle$,
the energy variances are
$$\operatorname{Var}_{Ue_{n}}(H_f)=n\bigl(\overline{\varepsilon^{2}}-\bar\varepsilon^{2}\bigr),\qquad \operatorname{Var}_{U\psi_{z}}(H_f)=|z|^{2}\,\overline{\varepsilon^{2}} ;$$
the first is strictly positive for every $n\ge1$ and the second is strictly
positive for every $z\ne0$, so neither preparation has sharp energy;

(e) *continuum thermal limitation*: the bounded operator $e^{-\beta H_f}$ is
not compact and hence not trace class for any $\beta>0$; consequently there is
no canonical-equilibrium preparation
$\rho_{\beta}=e^{-\beta H_f}/\operatorname{tr}e^{-\beta H_f}$ of the full
transverse continuum radiation sector. A normalised thermal preparation of the
model requires a separately declared mode selection or regularisation (for
instance a declared finite or summable mode family) and is not supplied by
this theorem; no thermal interpretation of any state is asserted here;

(f) all assertions are conditional on P1, P2 and the adopted radiation model
and use only the declared ideal counting model. No measured count, frequency,
efficiency or temperature is asserted, and no sampling model is introduced.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** the postulates P1, P2 and the adopted radiation model with transverse space $\mathfrak h$, Fock space $F(\mathfrak h)$, sectors $\mathfrak H_{n}^{+}$, projections $\Pi_{n}$, number operator $N$, energy $H_f$ with $\varepsilon(k)=\hbar c|k|$, a unit mode vector $\varphi$, a label $z\in\mathbb C$ and the isometry $U=U_\varphi$.

[F1] **Fixed-mode isometry.** $Ue_{n}=\varphi^{\otimes n}\in\operatorname{ran}P_{+}^{(n)}$, $(Ue_{m},Ue_{n})$ is orthonormal, $\|U\psi\|=\|\psi\|$, $NU\psi=UN'\psi$ for $\psi\in D(N')$, $A_-(\varphi)U\psi=UA_-(1)\psi$ for $\psi\in D(A_-(1))$, and for the transverse case with $\varphi\in D(\varepsilon_{\mathfrak h})$, $\langle H_fUe_{n},Ue_{n}\rangle=n\langle\varepsilon_{\mathfrak h}\varphi,\varphi\rangle$ and $\langle H_fU\psi,U\psi\rangle=\bigl(\sum_nn|\psi_n|^{2}\bigr)\langle\varepsilon_{\mathfrak h}\varphi,\varphi\rangle$ for $\sum_nn^{2}|\psi_n|^{2}<\infty$ ([[lem-nrqm-photons-fixed-mode-number-isometry]] clauses (a),(b),(d)).

[F2] **Fock sectors and number atoms.** $\Pi_{n}$ is the orthogonal projection onto the coordinate-$n$ subspace, the ranges are pairwise orthogonal with strong sum $I$, and for the number operator $N$ one has $N\iota_{n}(u)=n\iota_{n}(u)$ for every $u\in\mathfrak H_{n}^{+}$; the count law of the declared ideal total-number detector is $p_{n}(\rho)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho\Pi_{n})$ ([[lem-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-fock-sector-projections]], [[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-number-operator-domain]] clause (b), [[def-nrqm-photons-framework-ideal-counting-and-detection-model]] clause (b)).

[F3] **Coherent vector coefficients.** $\psi_{z}=e^{-|z|^{2}/2}\sum_{n}\frac{z^{n}}{\sqrt{n!}}e_{n}$ is unit with $\langle e_{n},\psi_{z}\rangle=e^{-|z|^{2}/2}\frac{\bar z^{n}}{\sqrt{n!}}$ and $|\langle e_{n},\psi_{z}\rangle|^{2}=e^{-|z|^{2}}\frac{|z|^{2n}}{n!}$ ([[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-fixed-mode-number-law]] clauses (b),(c)).

[F4] **Energy moments on mode sectors.** For a unit $\varphi\in D(\varepsilon_{\mathfrak h})$, with $\varepsilon_{n}(k_{1},\dots,k_{n})=\sum_{i}\varepsilon(k_{i})$, one has $\langle T_{n}\varphi^{\otimes n},\varphi^{\otimes n}\rangle=n\bar\varepsilon$; and if $\varphi\in D(\varepsilon_{\mathfrak h}^{2})$ then also $\langle T_{n}^{2}\varphi^{\otimes n},\varphi^{\otimes n}\rangle=n\,\overline{\varepsilon^{2}}+n(n-1)\bar\varepsilon^{2}$, with $\bar\varepsilon=\langle\varepsilon_{\mathfrak h}\varphi,\varphi\rangle$ and $\overline{\varepsilon^{2}}=\langle\varepsilon_{\mathfrak h}^{2}\varphi,\varphi\rangle$ ([[lem-nrqm-photons-fixed-mode-number-isometry]] clause (d)).

[F5] **Exponential series.** For every $x\ge0$, $\sum_{n}\frac{x^{n}}{n!}=e^{x}<\infty$, and the series converges absolutely ([[def-complex-exponential]], [[lem-complex-exponential-series-converges-everywhere]]).

[F6] **Non-compactness of the free Gibbs operator.** For every $\beta>0$ the operator $e^{-\beta H_f}$ is not compact and in particular not trace class ([[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-transverse-continuum-free-fock-hamiltonian]] clause (d)).

## Proof

1.1 [Number states] By [F1] each $Ue_{n}=\varphi^{\otimes n}$ is a unit vector of the sector $\operatorname{ran}P_{+}^{(n)}$; by [F2] $N$ acts on it as $n$ times itself, so the number readout is $n$ with probability one by the atom law of P2 ([[lem-nrqm-observables-spectral-measure-atoms-and-eigenvalues]]), and the count law of the declared detector is $p_{m}=\operatorname{tr}(T_{Ue_{n},Ue_{n}}\Pi_{m})=\langle\Pi_{m}Ue_{n},Ue_{n}\rangle=\delta_{mn}$. This proves (a). [F1, F2, algebra]

1.2 [Poisson law] For the mode-coherent preparation $U\psi_{z}$ the count law is $$p_{n}=\langle\Pi_{n}U\psi_{z},U\psi_{z}\rangle=\langle U\Pi_{n}'\psi_{z},U\psi_{z}\rangle=\langle\Pi_{n}'\psi_{z},\psi_{z}\rangle=|\langle e_{n},\psi_{z}\rangle|^{2}=e^{-|z|^{2}}\frac{|z|^{2n}}{n!},$$ using [F1] for the sector transfer and the isometry, and [F3] for the coefficient. [F1, F2, F3, algebra]

2.1 [Poisson moments] Put $x:=|z|^{2}\ge0$. By [F5], $\sum_{n\ge1}n\frac{x^{n}}{n!}=x\sum_{m\ge0}\frac{x^{m}}{m!}=xe^{x}$ and $\sum_{n\ge2}n(n-1)\frac{x^{n}}{n!}=x^{2}e^{x}$, so the mean is $e^{-x}xe^{x}=x$ and the second moment is $e^{-x}(x^{2}+x)e^{x}=x^{2}+x$; hence the variance is $x$. For $z\ne0$ the law is supported on more than one value, so the preparation is not a number state. This proves (b). [F3, F5, step 1.2, algebra]

3.1 [Energy means] The sector diagonality of $H_f$ and orthogonality of the sectors give, for the coherent preparation, $$\langle H_fU\psi_{z},U\psi_{z}\rangle=\sum_{n\in\mathbb N}|\langle e_{n},\psi_{z}\rangle|^{2}\,\langle T_{n}\varphi^{\otimes n},\varphi^{\otimes n}\rangle=\Bigl(\sum_{n}|\langle e_{n},\psi_{z}\rangle|^{2}n\Bigr)\bar\varepsilon=|z|^{2}\bar\varepsilon,$$ where the middle identity is [F1] and [F4] and the last is the Poisson mean of step 2.1; the number-state value is the $n$-th instance of [F1]. The mean exists because both sides are finite: $\bar\varepsilon<\infty$ by $\varphi\in D(\varepsilon_{\mathfrak h})$ and Cauchy-Schwarz, and $\sum_{n}n|\langle e_{n},\psi_{z}\rangle|^{2}=x<\infty$. This proves (c). [F1, F2, F4, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 [Energy variances] For the number state, $\langle H_f^{2}Ue_{n},Ue_{n}\rangle=\langle T_{n}^{2}\varphi^{\otimes n},\varphi^{\otimes n}\rangle=n\overline{\varepsilon^{2}}+n(n-1)\bar\varepsilon^{2}$ by [F4], so the variance is $n(\overline{\varepsilon^{2}}-\bar\varepsilon^{2})$, which is strictly positive for $n\ge1$ by clause (d) of [[lem-nrqm-photons-transverse-restricted-momentum-and-energy-multipliers]] (the energy multiplier has no eigenvalues, so $\overline{\varepsilon^{2}}-\bar\varepsilon^{2}=\operatorname{Var}_\varphi(\varepsilon)>0$). For the coherent preparation the sector-diagonal expansion gives $$\langle H_f^{2}U\psi_{z},U\psi_{z}\rangle=\sum_{n}|\langle e_{n},\psi_{z}\rangle|^{2}\bigl(n\overline{\varepsilon^{2}}+n(n-1)\bar\varepsilon^{2}\bigr)=x\,\overline{\varepsilon^{2}}+x^{2}\bar\varepsilon^{2},$$ using the Poisson first and second factorial moments of step 2.1; subtracting the square of the mean $x\bar\varepsilon$ from step 3.1 gives $x\overline{\varepsilon^{2}}$, which is strictly positive for $x=|z|^{2}>0$ because $\overline{\varepsilon^{2}}=\|\varepsilon_{\mathfrak h}\varphi\|^{2}>0$: $\varepsilon_{\mathfrak h}\varphi$ vanishes only where $\varphi$ vanishes off the null set $\{k=0\}$, so a unit $\varphi$ cannot satisfy $\varepsilon_{\mathfrak h}\varphi=0$ in $\mathfrak h$. This proves (d). [F1, F4, step 2.1, step 3.1, algebra]

5.1 [Thermal limitation and assembly] Clause (e) is [F6] read as a statement about the model's canonical-equilibrium form: a normalised preparation $\rho_{\beta}\propto e^{-\beta H_f}$ would require $e^{-\beta H_f}$ to be trace class, which [F6] excludes for every $\beta>0$. Steps 1.1 and 1.2 prove (a) and (b), steps 3.1 and 4.1 prove (c) and (d), and no step introduces a detector response, a sampling model or an empirical premise, which is (f). [F6, step 1.1, step 1.2, step 2.1, step 3.1, step 4.1] ∎

## Remarks

- **Poisson versus geometric.** The mode-coherent count law is Poisson, with
  variance equal to its mean; the declared single-mode Gibbs-type preparation
  of [[ex-nrqm-photons-single-mode-number-statistics-coherent-and-thermal]] has
  a geometric count law with larger variance at the same mean. Both are
  conditional model computations; distinguishing them in a laboratory requires
  a declared detector, preparation and sampling model and reported data.
- **No temperature.** The parameter $\beta$ in [F6] is a positive real
  parameter; its identification with an inverse temperature in $\mathrm J^{-1}$
  is an additional physical assumption not made here.
items.physical_scope: The conditional number and energy statistics of a declared normalisable mode of the adopted radiation sector: the n-quanta mode state has sharp count n; the mode-coherent state has the Poisson count law of parameter |z|^2 with mean and variance |z|^2; the energy means and variances of these preparations are computed from the mode profile, are strictly positive in variance, and the unregularised continuum free-field Gibbs operator is not trace class, so a thermal preparation requires a separately declared mode selection. The result is conditional on P1, P2 and the adopted radiation model, uses the ideal counting model only, reports no measured count and asserts no thermalisation.

items.title: Scope and empirical status of the photons and radiation modes page
items.statement:
## Scope of the page

**What the page adopts.** The page adopts the radiation extension of the
framework, [[post-nrqm-photons-radiation-extension-and-transverse-mode-assignment]]:
a fixed propagation-mode one-photon polarisation model with a two-dimensional
transverse internal space, a quantised free transverse radiation sector with
bosonic Fock space, and the mode assignments $\omega=c|k|$,
$E=\hbar\omega$ and $p=\hbar k$ in a declared inertial chart. These are
additional model assumptions of the framework; they are not derived from P1-P7,
not derived from classical Maxwell theory or special relativity, and not
obtained as a limit of the massive one-particle model. The page also adopts the
preparation and apparatus discipline P7
([[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]) and the observable and
probability postulate P2 ([[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]])
for every reading of a detector outcome.

**What the page proves conditionally.**
[[def-nrqm-photons-framework-fixed-mode-polarization-model]] and
[[def-nrqm-photons-framework-radiation-sector-and-quantum-assignments]] fix the
model vocabulary, units and domains.
[[pthm-nrqm-photons-fixed-mode-polarization-outcome-law]] proves the Born
outcome law $\cos^{2}(\theta-\varphi)$, $\sin^{2}(\theta-\varphi)$ of the
declared ideal analyser, its affinity over mixtures, its phase invariance and
the conditional update of a repeated ideal analyser.
[[pthm-nrqm-photons-one-photon-number-energy-and-momentum-laws]] proves that a
normalisable one-photon preparation has the sharp number readout one, the
energy law given by the push-forward of $\|f(k)\|^{2}\,d^{3}k$ under
$\hbar c|k|$, the corresponding momentum-component readouts, and strictly
positive energy and momentum variance.
[[pthm-nrqm-photons-fixed-mode-number-and-energy-statistics]] proves the sharp
count of the $n$-quanta mode state, the Poisson count law and moments of the
mode-coherent preparation, the energy means and variances of those
preparations, and the failure of the unregularised continuum free-field Gibbs
operator to be trace class. All these are conditional consequences of P1, P2
and the adopted radiation model; their units are recorded in
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]] and in the assigned observables
of the model.

**What the page does not claim.** The page does not derive the radiation
extension from Maxwell's equations, does not derive a Lorentz transformation
law for mode labels, polarisations or energies, and does not assert Galilean
covariance of the radiation sector; the two polarisation states of the photon
are adopted, and their relativistic description by Lorentz-group
representations is outside this non-relativistic extension. It does not
introduce a photon position wave function, a photon localisation operator or a
general photon-position distribution; the sharp-mode label $k$ is a spectral
parameter and not a state, and no normalisable one-photon vector has sharp
frequency, energy or momentum. It does not supply a light-matter Hamiltonian, a
dipole coupling, selection rules, absorption or stimulated emission, and it
does not supply vacuum spontaneous emission; those belong to the later pair
on light-matter and spectral transitions, where the coupling and environment
assumptions are declared separately.

**What the page's idealisations are.** The declared analyser, the declared
total-number detector and the declared energy-window detector are ideal
projection-valued measurements of the model
([[def-nrqm-photons-framework-ideal-counting-and-detection-model]]). No
laboratory polariser, counter or spectrometer is identified with them; no
efficiency, dark count, dead time, background, calibration or resolution is
declared, and a destructive absorption detector would require its own
instrument. A single measurement law is not a frequency: repeated trials
require a separately declared preparation and sampling model in the sense of
P7, which this page does not supply.

**Empirical status.** The page records no experiment, no measured count, no
calibration, no uncertainty budget and no statistical test, and none is
invented. The Born ratio $\cos^{2}(\theta-\varphi)$ of the declared analyser
coincides with the intensity ratio of the declared classical transverse-field
model of the companion page; the coincidence is a property of the two declared
models and does not establish field quantisation, and classical
electromagnetic waves also interfere. Whether a given source, polariser or
detector is described by the declared fixed-mode model is a tested
identification with uncertainty under P7; agreement of the model's conditional
predictions with reported data would be evidence about the combined model and
apparatus assumptions, not a deductive proof of the model or of the framework.

items.statement:
## Example

Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the observable and probability
postulate P2 ([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]]), the radiation extension
postulate clause (i)
([[post-nrqm-photons-radiation-extension-and-transverse-mode-assignment]]) and
the declared fixed-mode polarisation model
[[def-nrqm-photons-framework-fixed-mode-polarization-model]] with polarisation
space $V$, orthonormal basis $(e_{1},e_{2})$ and analyser projections
$P_{\theta}$. Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Fix an angle
$\theta\in\mathbb R$. This example compares two declared models of the same
analyser:

**(a) The quantised-model ratio.** Consider the pure one-photon polarisation
preparation of the ray $[e_{1}]$ and the declared ideal analyser at angle
$\theta$. By
[[pthm-nrqm-photons-fixed-mode-polarization-outcome-law]] the outcome law of
the analyser is
$$p_{+1}=\|P_{\theta}e_{1}\|^{2}=\cos^{2}\theta,\qquad p_{-1}=\sin^{2}\theta,$$
so the **transmitted Born probability** is $\cos^{2}\theta$ in the unit $1$ of
dimensionless probabilities.

**(b) The declared classical transverse-amplitude model.** Declare the
following elementary model, with no claim that it is Maxwell theory: its
**field data** are complex vectors $E\in V$, read as transverse field
amplitudes with an unspecified common dimension; the **analyser at angle
$\theta$** acts on the field data by the orthogonal projection
$$E\longmapsto P_{\theta}E;$$
the **declared intensity** of a field datum is
$$I(E):=\|E\|^{2},$$
and the model's **transmitted intensity fraction** is $I(P_{\theta}E)/I(E)$
for $E\ne0$. This is a declared idealisation of the classical description of a
polariser as projecting the transverse field amplitude (the Jones-vector
reading); it imports no Maxwell equation and makes no detector claim.

The example computes both ratios for the same declared data and compares them.

## Verification

**Given:** The declared polarisation space $V$ with orthonormal basis $(e_{1},e_{2})$, the analyser projections $P_{\theta},P_{\theta}^{\perp}$ and the angle $\theta$.

[L1] **Projection formulas.** $\langle e_{\theta},e_{1}\rangle=\cos\theta$, $P_{\theta}e_{1}=\cos\theta\,e_{\theta}$, $\|P_{\theta}e_{1}\|^{2}=\cos^{2}\theta$, and $\|P_{\theta}E\|^{2}=\langle E,P_{\theta}E\rangle$ for every $E\in V$ ([[lem-nrqm-photons-analyzer-projections-and-overlaps]] clauses (a),(b)).

[L2] **Born law of the analyser.** For the declared analyser and a pure preparation of unit vector $\psi$, the outcome probability is $\|P_{\theta}\psi\|^{2}$ ([[pthm-nrqm-photons-fixed-mode-polarization-outcome-law]] clause (c), [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (b)).

[L3] **Norm positivity.** For $E\ne0$ one has $I(E)=\|E\|^{2}>0$; and $I(cE)=|c|^{2}I(E)$ for $c\in\mathbb C$ ([[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]], [[lem-nrqm-photons-analyzer-projections-and-overlaps]] Fact [F1] of the inner-product conventions).

**Proof technique:** direct; evaluate the projection on $e_{1}$ and form the ratio of the squared norms.

**Given:** The data of the Example and [L1]-[L3].

1.1 [Quantised ratio] By [L1] the projectors satisfy $P_{\theta}e_{1}=\cos\theta\,e_{\theta}$ and hence $p_{+1}=\|P_{\theta}e_{1}\|^{2}=\cos^{2}\theta$; the complementary probability is $p_{-1}=1-p_{+1}=\sin^{2}\theta$. This is (a) read from the theorem of [L2]. [L1, L2, algebra]

1.2 [Classical ratio] Let $E\in V$, $E\ne0$. Applying [L1] with $E$ in place of $e_{1}$ gives $\|P_{\theta}E\|^{2}=\langle E,P_{\theta}E\rangle$; for the particular field datum $E=e_{1}$ this is $\|P_{\theta}e_{1}\|^{2}=\cos^{2}\theta$, and $I(e_{1})=\|e_{1}\|^{2}=1$ by [L1] and [L3]. Hence the declared transmitted intensity fraction is $$\frac{I(P_{\theta}e_{1})}{I(e_{1})}=\cos^{2}\theta .$$ [L1, L3, algebra]

2.1 [Comparison] Steps 1.1 and 1.2 show that the quantised model's transmitted Born probability and the declared classical model's transmitted intensity fraction coincide at $\cos^{2}\theta$ for the same declared angle and the same declared alignment $e_{1}$: the number $\cos^{2}\theta$ is common to the two declared models. Since the models disagree about what a preparation and an outcome are -- a unit ray with a Born law in the first model, a complex amplitude with a declared intensity in the second -- the coincidence of this ratio is not evidence for field quantisation, and the declared classical model is not refuted by a measurement of this ratio. This completes the announced computation. [step 1.1, step 1.2, algebra] ∎

## Remarks

- **What is compared.** Only the two declared models on the declared
  two-dimensional space are compared. No claim is made that the elementary
  classical model reproduces the photon counting statistics or the
  non-classical states of the radiation sector; the comparison of counting
  statistics is the subject of
  [[ex-nrqm-photons-single-mode-number-statistics-coherent-and-thermal]] and
  [[texp-nrqm-photons-classical-field-and-quantized-detection-comparison]].
- **Sources and status.** The coincidence of the classical transmitted
  fraction with the quantum transmitted probability is explicitly noted in the
  cited source; the classical model here is an elementary declared idealisation
  constructed for the comparison and is not a derivation from Maxwell theory.

The example establishes that the two declared models agree on this ratio and asserts no field quantisation, no detector claim, no Maxwell derivation and no empirical result.

items.title: Number statistics of a single declared mode: sharp, Poisson and geometric preparations
items.statement:
## Example

Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the observable and probability
postulate P2 ([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]]), the radiation extension
postulate
([[post-nrqm-photons-radiation-extension-and-transverse-mode-assignment]]),
the radiation sector definition
[[def-nrqm-photons-framework-radiation-sector-and-quantum-assignments]] and
the declared ideal counting model
[[def-nrqm-photons-framework-ideal-counting-and-detection-model]]. Assume the
Axioms of Countable Choice and of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Fix a unit mode vector $\varphi\in\mathfrak h$, write
$U=U_\varphi$ for the fixed-mode isometry of
[[lem-nrqm-photons-fixed-mode-number-isometry]] and let $z\in\mathbb C$ and a
**declared effective mode energy** $\varepsilon_{0}>0$ in joules (equivalently a
declared effective frequency $\omega_{0}=\varepsilon_{0}/\hbar>0$ in
$\mathrm s^{-1}$) be given parameters of this example. The example compares the
count statistics of the following three **declared preparations** of the mode
subspace, all read with the declared ideal total-number detector:

**(a) The $n$-quanta mode state.** For $n\in\mathbb N$, the pure preparation of
the ray of $Ue_{n}=\varphi^{\otimes n}$.

**(b) The mode-coherent state.** The pure preparation of the ray of
$U\psi_{z}$, with $\psi_{z}=e^{-|z|^{2}/2}\sum_{m}\frac{z^{m}}{\sqrt{m!}}e_{m}$.

**(c) The declared effective-energy mode preparation.** For a parameter
$\beta>0$ in $\mathrm J^{-1}$, the density operator
$$\rho_{\beta,\varepsilon_{0}}:=(1-q)\sum_{n\in\mathbb N}q^{n}\,T_{Ue_{n},Ue_{n}},\qquad q:=e^{-\beta\varepsilon_{0}}\in(0,1),$$
the transfer to the mode subspace of the single-mode weights of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-single-mode-thermal-trace]] with its parameter
$\omega$ set equal to the declared effective energy $\varepsilon_{0}$. This is
a declared conditional preparation of the model, not a derivation from any
radiation-matter interaction and not a statement that the mode is in thermal
equilibrium.

The example computes the count law, mean and variance of the three
preparations and compares them at equal mean.

## Verification

**Given:** The declared mode data: unit $\varphi\in\mathfrak h$, the isometry $U$, parameters $z\in\mathbb C$, $\varepsilon_{0}>0$, $\beta>0$, and the three preparations (a)-(c).

[L1] **Mode transfer and number law.** $Ue_{m}=\varphi^{\otimes m}$ are orthonormal unit vectors with $NUe_{m}=m\,Ue_{m}$, the count law of a preparation of $Ue_{m}$ is $\delta_{m}$, the count law of the mode-coherent preparation is $e^{-|z|^{2}}\frac{|z|^{2n}}{n!}$ with mean and variance $|z|^{2}$, and $\|\psi_{z}\|=1$ ([[pthm-nrqm-photons-fixed-mode-number-and-energy-statistics]] clauses (a),(b), [[lem-nrqm-photons-fixed-mode-number-isometry]] clauses (a),(b), [[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-fixed-mode-number-law]] clause (b)).

[L2] **Single-mode weights.** For the one-mode Fock space with orthonormal family $(e_{n})$, the weights $w_{n}:=e^{-\beta\omega n}$ satisfy $\sum_{n}w_{n}=(1-e^{-\beta\omega})^{-1}$ and $\sum_{n}n\,w_{n}=e^{-\beta\omega}(1-e^{-\beta\omega})^{-2}$, and $\rho_{\beta}=G_{\beta}/Z(\beta)$ is a density operator whose number expectation is $(e^{\beta\omega}-1)^{-1}$ ([[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-single-mode-thermal-trace]] clauses (b),(c),(d)).

[L3] **Geometric series.** For $q\in[0,1)$ one has $\sum_{n\ge0}q^{n}=(1-q)^{-1}$; for nonnegative double series the order of summation may be interchanged ([[thm-geometric-series]], [[thm-tonelli-for-nonnegative-double-series]]).

[L4] **States.** The rank-one operators $T_{u,u}$ of unit vectors are states, and a trace-norm convergent convex combination of states with weights $(1-q)q^{n}$, $\sum_{n}(1-q)q^{n}=1$, is a state ([[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]], [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]]).

**Proof technique:** direct; read the count law off the sector projections for (a) and (b), sum the geometric weights in (c), and compare the resulting means and variances.

**Given:** The data of the Example and [L1]-[L4].

1.1 [Sharp preparation] For the preparation (a) the count law is $p_{m}=\delta_{mn}$ by [L1]; its mean is $n$ and its variance $0$. [L1, algebra]

1.2 [Coherent preparation] For the preparation (b) the count law is Poisson by [L1], with mean and variance $|z|^{2}$; for $z=0$ it is the sharp law $\delta_{0}$. [L1, algebra]

1.3 [Effective-energy preparation is a state] By [L2] the weights satisfy $\sum_{n}q^{n}=(1-q)^{-1}$ with $q=e^{-\beta\varepsilon_{0}}$, so $(1-q)\sum_{n}q^{n}=1$ and the series defining $\rho_{\beta,\varepsilon_{0}}$ converges in trace norm; since each $T_{Ue_{n},Ue_{n}}$ is a state, the convex combination is a state by [L4]. Its count law is $p_{n}=\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{\beta,\varepsilon_{0}}\Pi_{n})=(1-q)q^{n}$ by the declared detector law and the orthogonality of the mode vectors. [L2, L4, algebra]

1.4 [Geometric moments] Put $p_{n}=(1-q)q^{n}$ with $0<q<1$. By [L3], $\sum_{n\ge1}n\,q^{n}=\sum_{k\ge1}\sum_{n\ge k}q^{n}=\sum_{k\ge1}\frac{q^{k}}{1-q}=\frac{q}{(1-q)^{2}}$, and likewise $\sum_{n\ge2}n(n-1)q^{n}=2\sum_{k\ge2}(k-1)\frac{q^{k}}{1-q}=\frac{2q^{2}}{(1-q)^{3}}$. Hence the mean, second moment and variance of the count law are $$\sum_{n}n\,p_{n}=\frac{q}{1-q}=\frac{1}{e^{\beta\varepsilon_{0}}-1},\qquad \sum_{n}n^{2}p_{n}=\frac{q(1+q)}{(1-q)^{2}},\qquad \operatorname{Var}=\frac{q}{(1-q)^{2}}=\frac{e^{\beta\varepsilon_{0}}}{(e^{\beta\varepsilon_{0}}-1)^{2}},$$ the variance formula from $\sum n^{2}p_{n}=2\sum_{n\ge2}\binom n2q^{n}(1-q)+\sum n p_{n}$ combined with the two sums above; in particular the variance equals $m(m+1)$ for the mean $m=(e^{\beta\varepsilon_{0}}-1)^{-1}$. [L3, algebra]

2.1 [Comparison at equal mean] By steps 1.2, 1.3 and 1.4, at the common mean $m=|z|^{2}=(e^{\beta\varepsilon_{0}}-1)^{-1}$ the coherent preparation has variance $m$ while the effective-energy preparation has variance $m(m+1)>m$, and the number-state preparation has variance $0$; the three declared preparations therefore assign different number fluctuations, and the comparison requires the same declared ideal counting model for all three. [step 1.1, step 1.2, step 1.3, step 1.4, algebra]

3.1 [Concluding comparison] The computations show: the $n$-quanta mode state has the sharp count $n$; the mode-coherent state has the Poisson count law with mean and variance $|z|^{2}$; and the declared effective-energy preparation with parameter $\varepsilon_{0}>0$ has the geometric law with mean $1/(e^{\beta\varepsilon_{0}}-1)$ and variance $m(m+1)$. The parameter $\varepsilon_{0}$ is declared; it is not derived from $\varphi$, because no normalisable mode vector has sharp energy. No measurement, sampling model or temperature identification occurs, and the comparison is a comparison of the declared conditional models, which is the announced computation. [step 1.1, step 1.2, step 1.3, step 1.4, step 2.1] ∎

## Remarks

- **Why the parameter is declared.** A normalisable mode vector has no sharp
  frequency or energy ([[pthm-nrqm-photons-one-photon-number-energy-and-momentum-laws]]
  clause (d)), so the geometric preparation cannot be obtained by evaluating a
  Gibbs density $e^{-\beta H_f}$ on the mode subspace; the effective energy
  $\varepsilon_{0}$ is a declared parameter of the example, and clause (e) of
  [[pthm-nrqm-photons-fixed-mode-number-and-energy-statistics]] records that
  the unregularised continuum free-field Gibbs operator is not trace class.
- **Counts are model quanta.** All three laws are laws of the declared ideal
  total-number detector; a laboratory photon-counting comparison would require
  a declared counter response, efficiency and sampling model, and reported
  data. None is supplied or assumed here.
items.physical_scope: A conditional computation of the count statistics of three declared preparations of one normalisable mode: the sharp count of an n-quanta mode state, the Poisson count law of the mode-coherent preparation, and the geometric count law of a declared effective-mode-energy Gibbs-type preparation. The example is conditional on P1, P2 and the adopted radiation model, declares its mode-energy parameter explicitly, records no measurement, no sampling model and no temperature identification, and asserts no thermalisation.

items.title: A two-bin comparison of a declared classical field model and the quantised model: identical normalised laws do not discriminate
items.statement:
## Statement

Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the observable and probability
postulate P2 and the preparation and apparatus discipline P7
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]), the radiation extension
postulate clause (i)
([[post-nrqm-photons-radiation-extension-and-transverse-mode-assignment]]) and
the declared fixed-mode polarisation model
[[def-nrqm-photons-framework-fixed-mode-polarization-model]] with polarisation
space $V$ and orthonormal basis $(e_{1},e_{2})$. Assume the Axioms of Countable
Choice and of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]).
Declare the following **two-bin comparison**:

1. an orthonormal pair $(u_{+},u_{-})$ of $V$, read as the pair of orthogonal
   **fringe bin directions** of a declared two-bin detector, with projections
   $Q_{\pm}x:=\langle x,u_{\pm}\rangle u_{\pm}$;
2. a **declared amplitude datum** $a\in V\setminus\{0\}$;
3. the **declared classical field model**, whose state datum is the amplitude
   $a$, whose bin intensities are $I_{\pm}(a):=\|Q_{\pm}a\|^{2}$, and whose
   normalised two-bin law is $I_{\pm}(a)/(I_{+}(a)+I_{-}(a))$;
4. the **quantised model reading** of the same datum: the pure preparation of
   the ray $[a]$ of the polarisation space, measured by the declared ideal
   sharp measurement with outcome projections $(Q_{+},Q_{-})$ in the sense of
   [[def-nrqm-photons-framework-ideal-counting-and-detection-model]] clause (d)
   with the Born law of P2.

Then:

(a) $Q_{+}+Q_{-}=I$ and the normalised stated laws of the two declared models
coincide for every datum $a\ne0$:
$$\frac{I_{\pm}(a)}{I_{+}(a)+I_{-}(a)}=p_{\pm}([a])=\frac{\|Q_{\pm}a\|^{2}}{\|a\|^{2}}=\frac{|\langle u_{\pm},a\rangle|^{2}}{\|a\|^{2}};$$

(b) writing $a=a_{1}+a_{2}$ for any declared decomposition of the datum into
two **path components**, both declared laws contain the interference
cross-term
$$2\operatorname{Re}\bigl(\langle u_{\pm},a_{1}\rangle\,\overline{\langle u_{\pm},a_{2}\rangle}\bigr),$$
so the presence of a fringe pattern of this two-bin form does not distinguish
the two declared models;

(c) the two declared models are nevertheless different physical models: in the
classical model the datum is a field amplitude with a deterministic intensity,
while in the quantised model it is a state ray with a Born law; a discriminator
must therefore be a prediction on which the two models differ -- for instance
the count statistics of a declared number detector on a declared number state
-- together with a declared detector response, preparation and sampling model
in the sense of P7;

(d) this item constructs no such discriminating comparison and reports no
data; it asserts no measurement, no count, no frequency and no empirical
conclusion, and it does not claim that the classical model agrees with the
quantised model beyond the declared two-bin law.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The declared polarisation space $V$ with orthonormal basis $(e_{1},e_{2})$, the orthonormal bin pair $(u_{+},u_{-})$, the projections $Q_{\pm}$, the datum $a\in V\setminus\{0\}$, and the two declared models.

[F1] **Projections and resolution.** For every orthonormal pair $(u_{+},u_{-})$ of the two-dimensional space $V$, the maps $Q_{\pm}$ are orthogonal projections with ranges $\mathbb Cu_{\pm}$, $Q_{+}Q_{-}=0$ and $Q_{+}+Q_{-}=I$ ([[lem-nrqm-photons-analyzer-projections-and-overlaps]] clauses (a),(d), applied with $(e_{1},e_{2}):=(u_{+},u_{-})$).

[F2] **Parseval.** For every $x\in V$ one has $\|x\|^{2}=\|Q_{+}x\|^{2}+\|Q_{-}x\|^{2}$ ([[thm-parseval-equivalences-for-a-complete-orthonormal-family]], [F1]).

[F3] **Born law.** For the declared ideal sharp measurement with outcome projections $(Q_{+},Q_{-})$ and the pure preparation of a unit vector $\psi$, the outcome probabilities are $\|Q_{\pm}\psi\|^{2}$; for a nonzero datum $a$ the unit vector is $\psi=a/\|a\|$ and the probabilities are $\|Q_{\pm}a\|^{2}/\|a\|^{2}$ ([[pthm-nrqm-photons-fixed-mode-polarization-outcome-law]] clause (c), [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (b), [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]]).

[F4] **Inner product.** The inner product is linear in the first argument and conjugate-linear in the second; consequently $\|Q_{\pm}a\|^{2}=|\langle u_{\pm},a\rangle|^{2}$, and for $a=a_{1}+a_{2}$,
$$|\langle u_{\pm},a\rangle|^{2}=|\langle u_{\pm},a_{1}\rangle|^{2}+|\langle u_{\pm},a_{2}\rangle|^{2}+2\operatorname{Re}\bigl(\langle u_{\pm},a_{1}\rangle\overline{\langle u_{\pm},a_{2}\rangle}\bigr)$$
([[lem-nrqm-photons-analyzer-projections-and-overlaps]] Fact [F1], [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]]).

[F5] **Identification discipline.** The claim that a laboratory source, interferometer or detector realizes one of the declared models is a tested identification with uncertainty in the sense of P7 ([[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]).

## Proof

1.1 [Resolution and normalised classical law] By [F1] the bin projections resolve the identity, $Q_{+}+Q_{-}=I$. For $a\ne0$ put $N(a):=I_{+}(a)+I_{-}(a)$; by [F2] applied to $a$ one has $N(a)=\|Q_{+}a\|^{2}+\|Q_{-}a\|^{2}=\|a\|^{2}>0$, so the normalised classical law is well defined and equals $I_{\pm}(a)/\|a\|^{2}=|\langle u_{\pm},a\rangle|^{2}/\|a\|^{2}$ by [F4]. [F1, F2, F4, algebra]

2.1 [Quantised law] The ray $[a]$ is a pure preparation; by [F3] the Born probabilities of the declared measurement with projections $(Q_{+},Q_{-})$ are $p_{\pm}=\|Q_{\pm}a\|^{2}/\|a\|^{2}=|\langle u_{\pm},a\rangle|^{2}/\|a\|^{2}$. Together with step 1.1 this proves (a). [F3, F4, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 [Common cross-term] Let $a=a_{1}+a_{2}$ be any decomposition. By [F4], both $I_{\pm}(a)=|\langle u_{\pm},a\rangle|^{2}$ and $p_{\pm}=\|a\|^{-2}|\langle u_{\pm},a\rangle|^{2}$ contain the displayed cross-term with the same coefficients, because the classical normalisation divides by the constant $\|a\|^{2}$, which is independent of the bin index. Hence the fringe contribution of the declared decomposition appears in both declared laws with the same functional form; this proves (b). [F4, step 1.1, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 [Why the comparison does not discriminate and what would] Steps 1.1 and 2.1 show equality of the two declared normalised two-bin laws for every datum; the equality of one class of predictions of two distinct models is not evidence for either, and it does not establish field quantisation. The models differ in their objects and in their assignments elsewhere: the classical model carries a deterministic intensity and no count law, whereas the quantised model assigns the sharp count law of a number state and the Poisson law of a coherent state under the declared number detector ([[pthm-nrqm-photons-fixed-mode-number-and-energy-statistics]] clauses (a),(b)). A discriminating comparison must therefore be designed on a prediction where the two declared models differ, with the detector response, preparation and sampling model declared in the sense of [F5]; no such comparison is constructed here and no data is reported. This proves (c) and (d). [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.1, F5] ∎

## Remarks

- **Classical waves interfere.** The cross-term of clause (b) is present in the
  declared classical intensity as well as in the Born law, so an interference
  pattern alone is not a signature of the quantised model and does not refute
  the declared classical model; conversely, the declared quantised model
  predicts the pattern too, so the absence of a visible pattern in finitely
  many detections would not by itself falsify it. Statistical comparison
  requires the sampling model of P7 and reported data.
- **What "classical" means here.** The classical model of this item is the
  elementary declared transverse-amplitude model with intensity equal to
  squared amplitude norm; it is not Maxwell's theory, and the item imports no
  Maxwell theorem. A test of classical electromagnetism would require that
  framework's own postulates and field solutions.
items.physical_scope: A conditional two-model comparison on a declared two-dimensional transverse amplitude space: the normalised two-bin laws assigned by a declared classical field model with intensity equal to squared amplitude norm and by the quantised fixed-mode model with the Born law for the same declared bin projections. The result is that the normalised laws coincide for every declared amplitude, so such a pattern does not discriminate the two declared models; the thought experiment records the cross-term (interference) structure common to both and asserts no experiment, no counts, no detector response and no empirical conclusion.

## Scope of the examples page

**What the three items establish.**
[[ex-nrqm-photons-malus-and-jones-analyzer-ratios]] shows that the Born
probability $\cos^{2}\theta$ of the declared ideal analyser on the preparation
along $e_{1}$ and the transmitted intensity fraction $\cos^{2}\theta$ of the
declared elementary classical transverse-amplitude model coincide for every
declared angle, so that this ratio alone does not establish field
quantisation. [[ex-nrqm-photons-single-mode-number-statistics-coherent-and-thermal]]
computes the count laws and their means and variances for three declared
preparations of one mode -- sharp $n$, Poisson with mean and variance
$|z|^{2}$, and the geometric law of a declared effective-energy preparation
with mean $1/(e^{\beta\varepsilon_{0}}-1)$ -- and shows that the fluctuation
content differs at equal mean.
[[texp-nrqm-photons-classical-field-and-quantized-detection-comparison]]
proves that the declared classical and quantised models assign the same
normalised two-bin law, with the same interference cross-term, for every
declared amplitude datum, and concludes that a two-bin fringe law of that form
is not a discriminator between the two declared models.

**What they rest on.** All three items are conditional on the state and
composition postulate P1, the observable and probability postulate P2, the
adopted radiation extension and the declared fixed-mode or radiation-sector
vocabulary of the main page; the counting results use only the declared ideal
total-number detector of
[[def-nrqm-photons-framework-ideal-counting-and-detection-model]]. The
classical models appearing in the first and third items are explicit
elementary declared models -- a complex transverse amplitude with intensity
equal to squared amplitude norm -- and are not Maxwell's theory; the effective
mode energy $\varepsilon_{0}$ of the second item is a declared parameter, not a
sharp energy of a normalisable mode.

**Different objects.** A one-photon preparation is a unit ray of the
transverse one-particle space read in the one-photon sector; a mode-coherent
preparation is a unit ray of the radiation Fock space with no sharp number;
and the declared classical intensity datum is a complex transverse amplitude
with its declared intensity. The three are distinct mathematical objects of
the declared models, and no identification of one with another is made.

**What is not claimed.** The page records no experiment, no apparatus, no
calibration, no measured count, no frequency, no efficiency and no uncertainty
budget, and none is invented. It does not claim that any laboratory polariser,
counter or interferometer realizes the declared ideal models; that claim is a
tested identification with uncertainty under P7
([[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]). It does not assert
thermal equilibrium or a temperature for the geometric preparation, and it
does not assert that the coincidence of the classical and quantum ratios is
evidence for field quantisation. Single-photon polarisation and counting
experiments remain research candidates for a separate reported-experiment
item; a finite sample of detections is a random object under any declared
sampling model, visible fringes can fail to appear with nonzero probability
under a correct coherent model, and a $p$-value or confidence level is not the
probability that a model is false. Comparing any of these conditional
predictions with data would test the combined model and apparatus assumptions,
not prove the model or the framework.
